401: 
402: ## Host Behavior (src/bun/index.ts — ~245 lines)
403: 
404: ### Startup Sequence
405: 1. `findProjectRoot(import.meta.dir)` — walks up directory tree until `package.json` found. Works in both dev and bundled modes.
406: 2. `baseDir = findProjectRoot(...)` — store the project root absolute path
407: 3. Resolve path function: `resolvePath(p)` — if relative, join with baseDir; absolute as-is; bare name (bun/python3) returned unmodified
408: 4. Spawn system plugins via `spawnPlugin()` — hardcoded plugins core-manifest and core-static spawned first (they are needed for user plugin discovery)
409: 5. Call `core-manifest.scan` via `routeRequest()` — returns user plugin manifests with `run` field
410: 6. For each user manifest with `run`:
411:    a. Split `run` by whitespace → `[cmd, ...args]`
412:    b. `Bun.spawn([cmd, ...args], { stdin: "pipe", stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" })`
413:    c. Store as `PluginInstance { config: manifest, process: proc, alive: true }`
414:    d. Start `readStream()` on both stdout + stderr with appropriate callbacks
415:    e. `proc.exited.then(code => { plugin.alive = false })` — marks dead on exit
416: 7. Define RPC handlers via `BrowserView.defineRPC()` — 3 request handlers (see RPC table)
417: 8. `getMainViewUrl()` — checks Vite HMR on port 5173 (in dev channel), returns dev URL if available, else starts inline `Bun.serve()` that serves `dist/`
418: 9. `new BrowserWindow({ title, url, frame, rpc })` — create the app window
419: 10. `setInterval()` — health check every 5 seconds (logs dead plugins, no auto-restart)
420: 11. `process.on("SIGINT")` — stop server, kill all plugin processes, exit
421: 
422: ### RPC Handlers
423: 
424: All handlers use `(params: unknown) =>` with internal casts.
425: 
426: | Handler | Params (cast from unknown) | Returns |
427: |---------|---------------------------|---------|
428: | `pluginRequest` | `{ method: string, params: any }` | `{ success, data?, error? }` |
429: | `resolveHook` | `{ hook: string }` | `{ success, data: { name, methods } }` or `{ success: false, error }` |
430: | `callHook` | `{ hook: string, method?: string, params: any }` | `{ success, data? }` or `{ success: false, error }` |
431: 
432: **RPC details:**
433: - `pluginRequest(method, params)`: calls `routeRequest(method, params)` which splits method by `.` — first part is plugin name, rest is action. Finds plugin by `config.name`, sends `{id, method: action, params}` via stdin. Returns Promise with 10s timeout.
434: - `resolveHook({ hook })`: finds first plugin with `config.hooks.includes(hook)`. Returns `{name, methods}`.
435: - `callHook({ hook, method?, params })`: finds plugin for hook, calls `routeRequest(name.method, params)`. Defaults to `methods[0]` if no method specified.
436: 
437: ### stdout/stderr Reader (readStream)
438: - Single generic async reader: `readStream(stream, name, onLine)`
439: - Web Streams API: `stream.getReader()`
440: - Buffers partial lines across chunks (split by `\n`, keep incomplete line in buffer via `lines.pop()`)
441: - Each complete line passed to `onLine` callback
442: - Used for both stdout (response parsing) and stderr (console logging)
443: 
444: ### Response Handling (handlePluginResponse)
445: 1. `JSON.parse(line)` → get `msg`
446: 2. Match by `msg.id` to pending request
447: 3. `clearTimeout(timer)` + `pendingRequests.delete(id)`
448: 4. `msg.error` exists → `reject(new Error(msg.error))`
449: 5. Else → `resolve(msg.result)`
450: 
451: ### Health Check
452: - `setInterval()` every 5000ms
453: - Logs dead plugins (no auto-restart)
454: 
455: ### Cleanup
456: - `process.on("SIGINT")` — kills all plugin subprocesses, stops static server
457: 
458: ---
459: 
460: ## Frontend Behavior (src/mainview/App.tsx — ~102 lines)
461: 
462: ### Imports & Setup
463: - `useState, useEffect` from React
464: - `Electroview` from electrobun/view (Electrobun's browser-side RPC bridge)
465: - Type imports: `PluginManifest` from shared/types
466: - NO `useRef` — UI plugin elements created imperatively, not via React refs
467: 
468: ### RPC Configuration
469: ```typescript
470: const electroview = new Electroview({
471:   rpc: Electroview.defineRPC({
472:     maxRequestTime: 20000,  // MUST be >= all inner timeouts combined
473:     handlers: { requests: {}, messages: {} },
474:   }),
475: })
476: ```
477: - `maxRequestTime: 20000` is CRITICAL. Host has 15000ms, routeRequest has 10s, plugin has 8s.
478:   Frontend timeout must be the largest (20s) because it's the outermost caller.
479: 
480: ### Global Bridges (module-level, outside App component)
481: ```typescript
482: window.__pluginRpc = async (method: string, params: any) => {
483:   const res = await electroview.rpc?.request.pluginRequest({ method, params })
484:   if (!res.success) throw new Error(res.error || "RPC error")
485:   return res.data
486: }
487: ```
488: - Any WC can call `window.__pluginRpc(method, params)` without importing Electrobun
489: - No `host.*` routing — bridge only routes to plugin subprocesses
490: - Method format: `"name.action"` (e.g., `"yt-feed.feed"`) — host splits on first dot to find plugin by name
491: 
492: ```typescript
493: window.resolveHook = async (hook: string) => {
494:   const res = await electroview.rpc.request.resolveHook({ hook })
495:   if (!res.success) throw new Error(res.error || "Hook resolution failed")
496:   return res.data
497: }
498: window.callHook = async (hook: string, methodOrArgs: any, args?: any) => {
499:   const method = args !== undefined ? methodOrArgs : undefined
500:   const params = args !== undefined ? args : methodOrArgs
501:   const res = await electroview.rpc.request.callHook({ hook, method, params })
502:   if (!res.success) throw new Error(res.error || "callHook failed")
503:   return res.data
504: }
505: ```
506: - `resolveHook(hook)` → finds plugin providing that hook (e.g., `"feed.video"` → yt-feed)
507: - `callHook(hook, method?, args)` → resolves hook + calls plugin method
508: 
509: ### App Component — State
510: - `manifests` — array of `PluginManifest` from `getPluginManifests` RPC
511: 
512: ### On Mount — Init Function
513: ```typescript
514: useEffect(() => { init().catch(e => { ... }) }, [])
515: ```
516: `init()` does:
517: 1. Fetches manifests via `electroview.rpc.request.getPluginManifests({})`
518: 2. For each manifest, collects WC tags from `feeds[].card` and `ui` (dedup by tag)
519: 3. Loads each frontend JS via `getPluginFrontend({ path: "build/plugins/<tag>.js" })`
520:    - `path` starts with `build/plugins/` (NOT `plugins/x/frontend/y.js`)
521:    - Restricted to `build/plugins/` directory by host security check
522: 4. Builds `uiPlugins[]` array — all manifests with `ui` field
523: 5. For each UI plugin: waits for WC definition, creates element imperatively, sets `.manifests = all`, appends to `#feed-container`
524:    - Creates elements for ALL UI plugins (not just last one)
525:    - Uses `document.getElementById("feed-container")` — not React refs
526: 
527: ### Render
528: ```typescript
529: return (
530:   <div className="...">
531:     <h1>Electro Plugins</h1>
532:     <div id="feed-container" />
533:   </div>
534: )
535: ```
536: - Only renders a container div — UI plugin elements are created imperatively inside it
537: - No React refs to web components — elements managed via `document.getElementById`
538: - No `<feed-widget>` in JSX — created imperatively
539: 
540: ---
541: 
542: ## Build System
543: 
544: `scripts/build-plugins.ts` (~191 lines) — centralized build for all plugin frontends.
545: 
546: ### How It Works
547: 1. Scans `plugins/` recursively via `findPluginDirs()` — finds all directories containing `plugin.json` (supports nested plugins like `plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-card/`)
548: 2. For each plugin dir, reads `plugin.json` and collects WC tag names from:
549:    - `manifest.ui` (single tag, e.g., `"feed-widget"`)
550:    - `manifest.components[]` (array of tags, e.g., `["yt-video-card"]`)
551:    - `manifest.feeds[*].card` (card tags from each feed contribution, e.g., `"yt-video-card"`)
552: 3. Deduplicates tags across plugins (`new Set()`)
553: 4. For each unique tag:
554:    a. Finds source file: checks `<dir>/<tag>.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte` in order
555:    b. If not found in plugin's dir, skips (defers to plugin that declares it — cross-directory ownership via `components` field)
556:    c. Reads source content to auto-detect framework (React vs Preact) via import string matching
557:    d. Generates a temporary `.vite.config.mjs`, `entry.tsx` (with WC boilerplate), and `style.css`
558:    e. Runs `bunx vite build --config <configFile>` targeting IIFE format
559:    f. Output: `build/plugins/<tag>.js` (deleted temp files after build)
560: 5. Framework auto-detection: reads source file, checks for `"react"`/`"react-dom"` imports (React) vs `"preact"`/`"preact/hooks"` (Preact). Falls back to first match if ambiguous.
561: 
562: ### Entry Template (React example)
563: Generated by the build script's `entry()` function:
564: ```typescript
565: import Component from "./yt-video-card.tsx"
566: import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client"
567: customElements.define("yt-video-card", class extends HTMLElement {
568:   root = null
569:   _item = null
570:   _manifests = null
571:   connectedCallback() { this.root = createRoot(this); this._render() }
572:   disconnectedCallback() { this.root?.unmount(); this.root = null }
573:   set item(d) { this._item = d; this._render() }
574:   set manifests(d) { this._manifests = d; this._render() }
575:   _render() { this.root.render(<Component item={this._item} manifests={this._manifests} />) }
576: })
577: ```
578: - All WCs get `_item` and `_manifests` setters (even non-card WCs — harmless)
579: - CSS inlined via `vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js` (Tailwind classes included)
580: 
581: ### Tag Sources
582: | Manifest Field | Type | Purpose |
583: |---------------|------|---------|
584: | `ui: "feed-widget"` | string | Main UI WC (built + mounted by App.tsx) |
585: | `components: ["yt-video-card"]` | string[] | Built-only WCs (not mounted by App.tsx) |
586: | `feeds[i].card: "yt-video-card"` | string | Feed item card WCs (loaded, mounted by feed-widget) |
587: 
588: ### Cross-Directory Source Discovery
589: When a plugin references a WC tag (via `feeds[].card`) but the source file isn't in that plugin's directory:
590: - Build script logs `skip <tag> (source not found in <dir>)`
591: - The tag WILL be built if ANOTHER plugin declares it in `components[]` or `ui`
592: - Fix: Declare `components: ["<tag>"]` on the plugin that owns the source file
593: - Example: `plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-card/plugin.json` has `components: ["yt-video-card"]` — builds the source in its own directory
594: 
595: ### Entry Template Paths (at runtime, in App.tsx)
596: Frontend JS is loaded from `build/plugins/<tag>.js` via `getPluginFrontend({ path })`.
597: Previously: `plugins/<name>/frontend/<tag>.js`. Now: `build/plugins/<tag>.js`.
598: 
599: ### Run Commands
600: ```bash
601: bun run build:plugins          # Build all plugin frontends (output to build/plugins/)
602: bun run start                  # build:plugins + vite build + electrobun dev
603: ```
604: 
605: ### Framework Handling
606: | Framework | Source Ext | Build Tool | Bundle Size |
607: |-----------|-----------|------------|-------------|
608: | React | .tsx/.jsx | Vite (IIFE) | ~40KB + code |
609: | Preact | .tsx/.jsx | Vite (IIFE) | ~3KB + code |
610: | Vue | .vue | Vite (IIFE) | ~35KB + code |
611: | Svelte | .svelte | Vite (IIFE) | varies |
612: 
613: "Works forever" principle: framework code inlined into the plugin's .js file.
614: The plugin never depends on what version of React/Vue/Preact the host app uses.
615: 
616: ---
617: 
618: ## Plugin Manifest Schema (Current — Flat Format)
619: 
620: ```json
621: {
622:   "name": "yt-feed",
623:   "run": "bun plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/main.ts",
624:   "hooks": ["feed.video"],
625:   "methods": ["feed"],
626:   "feeds": [
627:     { "type": "video", "card": "yt-video-card" }
628:   ]
629: }
630: ```
631: 
632: ### Fields
633: | Field | Required | Description |
634: |-------|----------|-------------|
635: | `name` | ✅ | Unique plugin ID. Used in RPC routing, path derivation |
636: | `version` | ❌ | Semver version. |
637: | `description` | ❌ | Short description. |
638: | `author` | ❌ | Creator name. |
639: | `run` | ❌ | Command to spawn subprocess. Example: `"bun plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/main.ts"` |
640: | `methods` | ❌ | Array of method prefixes for direct RPC routing. Example: `["feed", "login", "logout", "status"]` |
641: | `hook` | ❌ | Alias for `hooks` (single string). Which hooks this plugin satisfies. |
642: | `hooks` | ❌ | Array of hook strings. Which hooks this plugin satisfies. Example: `["feed.video", "auth"]` |
643: | `ui` | ❌ | WC tag for main-UI rendering. Path: `build/plugins/<tag>.js`. App.tsx loads AND mounts this. |
644: | `components` | ❌ | Array of WC tag names that need building but are neither `ui` nor `feeds[].card`. Example: `["yt-video-card"]` |
645: | `feeds` | ❌ | Array of feed contribution objects. If present, this plugin is a feed source. |
646: | `feeds[].type` | ✅ (if feeds) | Content type: `"video"`, `"image"`, `"post"`, etc. Also used as default hook for resolution. |
647: | `feeds[].method` | ❌ | RPC method to call. Defaults to `methods[0]`. |
648: | `feeds[].card` | ❌ | WC tag for rendering one item. Path: `build/plugins/<tag>.js`. If absent, items skipped. |
649: 
650: ### Plugin Types
651: - **Backend-only**: Has `run` but no `ui`/`feeds` → spawned as subprocess, no UI
652: - **Frontend-only (main UI)**: Has `ui` but no `run` → WC loaded and mounted by App.tsx
653: - **Frontend-only (card/component)**: Has `components` or `feeds[].card` but no `run` → WC loaded by App.tsx, mounted by feed-widget
654: - **Fullstack**: Has `run` + `ui`/`feeds` → subprocess + frontend components
655: - **Feed source**: Has `run` + `feeds` → subprocess with feed method + card WC
656: 
657: **Frontend path derivation** (build time and runtime):
658: - Build script collects tags from: `ui`, `components[]`, `feeds[*].card`
659: - Output: `build/plugins/<tag>.js`
660: - Search: plugin's own directory first, then cross-directory fallback by tag name
661: 
662: ### Example Manifests
663: 
664: **yt-feed (feed source, backend + card)**:
665: ```json
666: {
667:   "name": "yt-feed",
668:   "run": "bun plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/main.ts",
669:   "hooks": ["feed.video"],
670:   "methods": ["feed"],
671:   "feeds": [{ "type": "video", "card": "yt-video-card" }]
672: }
673: ```
674: 
675: **yt-auth (auth provider, backend-only)**:
676: ```json
677: {
678:   "name": "yt-auth",
679:   "run": "bun plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-auth/main.ts",
680:   "hooks": ["auth"],
681:   "methods": ["login", "logout", "status"]
682: }
683: ```
684: 
685: **yt-card (component provider, frontend-only)**:
686: ```json
687: {
688:   "name": "yt-card",
689:   "components": ["yt-video-card"]
690: }
691: ```
692: 
693: **feed (main UI, frontend-only)**:
694: ```json
695: {
696:   "name": "feed",
697:   "description": "Aggregate content from all your plugins into a single feed",
698:   "author": "Me",
699:   "version": "1.0.0",
700:   "ui": "feed-widget"
701: }
702: ```
703: 
704: **video-player (fullstack with ui)**:
705: ```json
706: {
707:   "name": "video-player",
708:   "run": "bun plugins/video-player/main.ts",
709:   "hooks": ["player"],
710:   "methods": ["load"],
711:   "ui": "player-modal"
712: }
713: ```

717: ## Plugin Implementations
718: 
719: ### Phase 1/2 Demo Plugins (REMOVED FROM DISK — Historical Reference Only)
720: - **greet-go** — Go backend (greet.hello, greet.bye). Frontend (greet-widget) removed in Phase 3. REMOVED from disk.
721: - **logger-py** — Python backend (log.info, log.list). Frontend (log-viewer) removed in Phase 3. REMOVED from disk.
722: - **joke-fetcher** — Bun/TS backend (joke.random, joke.types). REMOVED from disk.
723: - **youtube-explorer** — Original monolithic YouTube plugin. Split into yt-feed, yt-auth, yt-search, yt-card. REMOVED from disk.
724: 
725: ### yt-feed — YouTube Feed Backend (Bun/TS)
726: 
727: #### Backend (plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/main.ts)
728: - Uses Innertube API for YouTube home feed
729: - Lazily loads cookie from shared file (`.youtube-cookie` written by yt-auth)
730:   - Cookie read at request time, not startup — catches file written by yt-auth after process start
731: - `feed` method: calls `tube.getHomeFeed()`, returns array of video items
732: - Methods are simple (no prefix): just `"feed"` — prefix added by feed-widget as `name + "." + method`
733: - 8s Promise.race timeout on API calls
734: - No `feeds.method` in manifest — defaults to `methods[0]` ("feed")
735: 
736: ### yt-auth — YouTube Cookie Auth (Bun/TS)
737: 
738: #### Backend (plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-auth/main.ts)
739: - Browser cookie database discovery:
740:   - Firefox: finds `cookies.sqlite` via `find ~/.mozilla -name "cookies.sqlite" 2>/dev/null`
741:   - Chrome/Chromium: tries sweet-cookie library, falls back to `find` for Cookies DB
742: - Copies DB to temp file (avoids SQLite locking issues)
743: - Queries: `SELECT name, value, host FROM moz_cookies WHERE host LIKE '%youtube.com'`
744: - Extracts SAPISID cookie → constructs SAPISIDHASH Authorization header
745: - Filters ST-* cookies (avoids 413 Request Entity Too Large on YouTube API)
746: - Writes cookie to shared `.youtube-cookie` file (read by yt-feed)
747: - Methods: `login` (discover+write), `logout` (delete file), `status` (check file exists)
748: 
749: ### yt-card — YouTube Video Card WC (React, no backend)
750: 
751: #### Frontend (plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-card/yt-video-card.tsx)
752: - React card WC built via esbuild entry template
753: - Receives item prop: `{ thumbnail, title, channel, viewCount, published }`
754: - Renders thumbnail img, title H3, channel, views, published date
755: - Handles click on thumbnail → calls `window.__pluginRpc("video-player.load", {url, title})` then dispatches `new CustomEvent("player-load", {detail: {url, title}})` on window
756: - Player-modal listens for `player-load` to auto-open
757: - Manifest uses `components: ["yt-video-card"]` — built but NOT mounted as top-level view
758: 
759: ### yt-search — YouTube Search Backend (Bun/TS)
760: 
761: #### Backend (plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-search/main.ts)
762: - Uses Innertube API for YouTube search
763: - `search` method: takes query param, calls `tube.search()`, returns results
764: 
765: ### feed-widget — Feed Orchestrator WC (React, no backend)
766: 
767: #### Frontend (plugins/feed/feed-widget.tsx)
768: - 5-state machine: `loading` (spinner), `error` (system error), `empty` (no sources), `partial` (some errors), `loaded` (all ok)
769: - Loads feed via `callHook("feed.video")` — uses hook resolution, not direct source.feeds.method calls
770: - Uses `name + "." + method` RPC prefix: calls `__pluginRpc(source.name + "." + source.feeds[0].method)` = `__pluginRpc("yt-feed.feed")`
771: - Error banners per source with "Sign in" button:
772:   - Searches ALL manifests for a plugin with `methods.includes("login")` (not just errored source)
773:   - Shows sign-in button if such a plugin exists
774:   - Calls login method, reloads feed on success
775: - `CardRenderer`: creates card WCs via `document.createElement(tag)`, sets `.item`, appends to container
776: - Uses `customElements.whenDefined()` to wait for WC registration before creating elements
777: 
778: ### peertube — PeerTube Feed Backend + Card WC (Bun/TS + React)
779: 
780: #### Backend (plugins/peertube/main.ts)
781: - Fetches videos from a PeerTube instance API
782: - `list` method: returns array of video items from PeerTube instance
783: 
784: #### Frontend (plugins/peertube/peertube-card.tsx)
785: - React card WC similar to yt-video-card
786: - Handles click → dispatches `player-load` custom event with `{url, title}`
787: - Manifest: `feeds: [{type:"video", card:"peertube-card"}]`
788: 
789: ### video-player — Player Modal (Bun/TS + React WC)
790: 
791: #### Backend (plugins/video-player/main.ts)
792: - Lightweight backend, `load` method is a placeholder
793: - Manifest: `ui: "player-modal"`, `hooks: ["player"]`
794: 
795: #### Frontend (plugins/video-player/player-modal.tsx)
796: - Uses `<iframe>` (not `<video>`) — service embed URLs are HTML pages, not direct media files
797: - Listens for `"player-load"` custom event on `window` (dispatched by card WCs)
798: - On event: calls `__pluginRpc("load", {url})` and shows modal with iframe
799: - Handles close button, click-outside-to-close, Escape key
800: 
801: #### Data flow
802: 1. App.tsx calls host RPC → gets manifests → loads frontends from `build/plugins/<tag>.js`
803: 2. App.tsx creates UI WC elements imperatively in `#feed-container`, sets `.manifests = all`
804: 3. feed-widget's `.manifests` setter stores manifests, calls `loadFeed()`
805: 4. `loadFeed()`: for each source with `feeds[]`, calls `__pluginRpc(source.name + "." + method, {})`
806: 5. Results merged into flat `items[]` array
807: 6. `CardRenderer` creates WC for each item, sets `.item`, appends
808: 
809: #### __pluginRpc callers
810: - feed-widget calls `__pluginRpc(source.name + "." + method, {})` (e.g., `"yt-feed.feed"`)
811: - feed-widget calls `__pluginRpc(authPlugin.name + "." + method, {})` when user clicks "Sign in"
812: - Auth method found by searching ALL manifests for `methods.includes("login")`
813: - No host.* prefix — bridge is simple, routes only to plugin subprocesses
814:

816: 
817: ## All Key Decisions Made (Chronological)
818: 
819: ### Architecture Decisions
820: 1. **Language-agnostic plugin system** — plugins can be written in any language (Go, Python, etc.)
821: 2. **Subprocess stdin/stdout JSON-RPC** — simplest cross-language IPC. Each plugin is a standalone process
822: 3. **No `jsonrpc` field** — messages are `{"id", "method", "params"}` only, cleaner than full JSON-RPC spec
823: 4. **Host routes by method prefix** — `"greet."` matches `"greet.hello"`. Plugin handles the specific action
824: 5. **Desktop first, mobile later** — subprocess works on desktop. Mobile will need FFI/Wasm
825: 6. **Different skeleton per platform is fine** — Electrobun for desktop, Tauri/zero-native for mobile. Plugins don't change
826: 7. **Everything is a plugin** — including frontend UI and eventually the skeleton itself
827: 8. **No "core" plugin** — just feature plugins (no separate plugin for core system functionality)
828: 9. **Companion app** (future) — a tiny binary that reads config and launches the right skeleton for the platform
829: 10. **Manifest scanning from plugins/*/plugin.json** — replaced config.json. Host reads all plugin.json files at startup via readdirSync + JSON.parse. No central config needed.
830: 11. **Flat manifest format** — no nested backend/frontend objects. All fields at top level. Matches VS Code/Chrome/Obsidian conventions.
831: 
832: ### Framework Decisions
833: 12. **Electrobun for prototyping** — easiest for a beginner (Bun/TypeScript). Native WebView, ~14MB bundle, fast startup
834: 13. **Tauri for future mobile** — Rust, mature ecosystem, iOS + Android support, but requires learning Rust
835: 14. **zero-native** (Vercel Labs) — alternative future option. Zig + system WebView, mobile support, but pre-release (v0.2)
836: 15. **WebUI (webui-dev)** — interesting but no mobile path. Opens a real browser (Chrome/Firefox), not a WebView. Few KB library
837: 16. **React + Tailwind + Vite** for the frontend (from the Electrobun template)
838: 
839: ### Phase 3 Decisions
840: 17. **Feed approach is THE approach** — old per-plugin widget cards are dead. App.tsx mounts only `<feed-widget>`. No WebComponentSlot, no plugin cards, no callMethod, no result box.
841: 18. **No library sharing needed** — one WC class definition is shared across all DOM instances. Framework bundle lives in prototype. Different plugins have different bundles (their own versions). No duplication within the same WC type. Option B (per-plugin shared library) solves a non-problem.
842: 19. **No `host.*` routing** — feed-widget does NOT call host RPCs. App.tsx calls host directly (`electroview.rpc.request.getPluginManifests({})`) and passes data via `.manifests` setter on the WC DOM element. `__pluginRpc` bridge stays simple: routes only to plugin subprocesses.
843: 20. **No fallback cards** — postponed. Only cards from plugins are rendered. Items from plugins without `card` field are skipped.
844: 21. **Data flow via property setters** — App.tsx uses `.manifests` setter, feed-widget uses `.item` setter on each card. Not via RPC, not via events.
845: 22. **`_item` naming convention** — private backing field with underscore prevents infinite loop in setter. `set item(data) { this._item = data; this._render() }`. Getter: `get item() { return this._item }`.
846: 23. **Simplified manifest** — `run` replaces `command`+`args`. `feeds` block replaces `frontendComponent`/`frontendFile`/`frontendSlot`. `ui` field for main-UI WC (only feed plugin uses it). No backward compat with old format.
847: 24. **Path derivation** — frontend file paths NOT in manifest. Derived at runtime: `plugins/<name>/frontend/<tag>.js`. Tag comes from `ui` or `feeds.card` field.
848: 25. **Feed is a plugin** — `plugins/feed/` with no backend. Users can swap feed implementation by installing a different feed plugin.
849: 26. **Framework agnostic cards** — each card WC is self-contained IIFE with framework inlined. React, Preact, Vue, Svelte all work.
850: 27. **No schema** — feed doesn't know or care about item structure. Raw data passes through to card WC. Cards written by the same person as the backend.
851: 28. **Auth in error banners** — feed-widget shows "Sign in" button in per-plugin error banners when plugin has `.auth.login` method. Calls it, reloads feed on success.
852: 29. **5 feed states** — loading, system error, empty, partial (some errors), loaded (all ok). Error banners per-plugin.
853: 
854: ### Plugin Design Decisions
855: 17. **Web Components for frontend plugins** — any framework (React, Vue, Svelte, Angular) can compile to them. Browser standard, no framework lock-in
856: 18. **Iframes as alternative** — stronger isolation, separate JS context, communication via postMessage. Heavier. Cannot display native UI (Qt/GTK)
857: 19. **Three plugin types** — `backend` (subprocess only), `frontend` (Web Component only), `fullstack` (both)
858: 20. **`window.__pluginRpc()` global bridge** — simplest way for any WC framework to call backend. No imports needed.
859: 21. **Centralized build script** — `scripts/build-plugins.js` handles all plugin types. One command for all.
860: 22. **`findProjectRoot()` walks up from `import.meta.dir`** — works in both dev (flat) and bundled modes
861: 23. **FileSink.write() for plugin stdin** — Bun's `Subprocess.stdin` is a `FileSink` when piped. Use `.write()` directly.
862: 24. **RPC params typed as `unknown`** — Electrobun's `defineRPC` expects `(params?: unknown) => unknown`. All handlers cast internally.
863: 
864: ### Go Plugin Specific
865: 25. **`*json.RawMessage` for params** — user explicitly chose this over simpler `map[string]interface{}`. More type safety, more verbose.
866: 26. **Nested struct for params** — each method defines its own params struct, unmarshals from RawMessage
867: 
868: ### Teaching/Communication Decisions
869: 27. **User is a beginner** — assume ZERO prior knowledge. Explain every concept, syntax, and line
870: 28. **Provide full code in messages** — user copies code themselves. Never modify files without explicit permission
871: 29. **Line-by-line explanation tables** — after every code block, explain each section in a table
872: 30. **Multi-level zoom** — big picture → file → scope/block → line → symbol → syntax construct

882: ### Session 2026-07-07 Decisions (Plugin Refactor — youtube-explorer split, hooks, components, feeds array)
883: 39. **`components` manifest field** — separates build concern from mount concern. `ui` → build AND mount (views). `components` → build only (cards, sub-components). Fixes the Single-Field Conflation Antipattern where `ui` was the only way to trigger a build.
884: 40. **`hooks` manifest field** — decentralized capability discovery. A plugin declares what hooks it satisfies (e.g., `"feed.video"`, `"auth"`, `"search"`, `"player"`). The host resolves hooks at runtime. Replaces hardcoded method prefix routing for capability discovery.
885: 41. **`callHook`/`resolveHook` RPC handlers** — new host RPCs for hook-based discovery. `callHook` finds the first plugin matching a hook and calls its method. Enables feed-widget to use `callHook("feed.video")` instead of iterating manifests.
886: 42. **`feeds` as array** — `feeds: [{type:"video", card:"yt-video-card"}]` (was a single object). Enables a single plugin to contribute to multiple feed types. The `feeds-as-array` future plan is now implemented.
887: 43. **Plugin nesting** — plugins can live under other plugins: `plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/`. The host uses recursive directory scanning (`getAllPluginManifests`). Parent `plugin.json` (youtube) has metadata only. Enables logical grouping.
888: 44. **Monolithic plugin split** — `youtube-explorer` (one big plugin) split into `yt-feed`, `yt-auth`, `yt-search`, `yt-card`. Each has a single responsibility. yt-feed handles feed, yt-auth handles auth, yt-search handles search, yt-card provides the video card WC.
889: 45. **Lazy cookie reload** — yt-feed re-reads cookie file on each request if `cookieStr` is null. Catches file written by yt-auth after startup. Fixes the "auth before feed" timing issue for long-lived processes.
890: 46. **`name + "." + method` RPC prefix** — feed-widget calls `__pluginRpc("yt-feed.feed")` instead of `__pluginRpc("feed")`. The host splits on first dot to find plugin by `config.name`. This is needed because simple method names ("feed", "list") would overlap between plugins.
891: 47. **Sign-in button searches ALL manifests** — feed-widget searches `manifests.find(m => m.methods?.includes("login"))` rather than checking only the errored source's methods. Auth methods live on a separate plugin (yt-auth) from the feed source (yt-feed).
892: 48. **`components` as declarative ownership** — when source not found in referencing dir, use `components` field on the owning plugin's manifest. yt-card declares `components: ["yt-video-card"]` so the build script finds the source in yt-card's directory.
893: 49. **Build output path changed** — frontend JS loads from `build/plugins/<tag>.js` (was `plugins/<name>/frontend/<tag>.js`). Centralized build output directory. Host security restricts `getPluginFrontend` to `build/plugins/` path.
894: 50. **Vite as universal build tool** — replaced ad-hoc esbuild-only approach. Now all frameworks (React, Preact, Vue, Svelte) build via Vite IIFE. Build script auto-detects framework by scanning imports in source files.
895: 51. **Build script entry template includes `_manifests`** — all WCs get both `_item` and `_manifests` setters. Allows any WC to access the full manifests array for self-discovery.
896: 52. **Player modal uses `<iframe>`** — embed URLs from YouTube/PeerTube are HTML pages, not direct media files. `<video>` tag cannot play them. iframe is the standard approach for embed URLs.
897: 53. **Event bridge for card→modal** — cards dispatch `CustomEvent("player-load", {detail: {url, title}})` on `window`. Player-modal listens in `useEffect(() => { window.addEventListener("player-load", handler) })`. Decoupled communication.
898: 54. **Plugin UI elements created imperatively** — App.tsx uses `document.getElementById("feed-container")` and `document.createElement(tag)` instead of React refs or JSX. WCs created outside React's VDOM to avoid framework conflicts.
899: 55. **No `frontend/` subdirectory** — source files alongside `plugin.json` (e.g., `plugins/feed/feed-widget.tsx`). The build script finds source by `<dir>/<tag>.<ext>`. Previously required `frontend/` subdirectory.
900: 56. **Recursive manifest scanning** — `getAllPluginManifests()` walks directory tree recursively. Supports nested plugins under `plugins/*/plugins/*/`. Flat scan (`readdirSync(plugins/*)`) doesn't find deeply nested manifests.

981: ### Bug #12 (CRITICAL): Frontend RPC timeout default too short for slow plugins
982: - **Location**: `src/mainview/App.tsx`, line 7 — `Electroview.defineRPC({})`
983: - **Problem**: `Electroview.defineRPC()` with no `maxRequestTime` defaults to a very short timeout (~1s). The youtube-explorer feed request takes ~2.5s (Innertube.create 1.3s + getHomeFeed 1.2s). The frontend's RPC timer fired before the plugin response arrived. The host received the response and resolved it (visible in terminal logs `handleResponse pending=true`), but the frontend had already thrown "RPC request timed out." — the response was discarded because nobody was listening.
984: - **Fix**: Added `maxRequestTime: 20000` to BOTH `BrowserView.defineRPC()` (host, was already 15000) AND `Electroview.defineRPC()` (frontend, was missing). The frontend timeout must be >= all inner timeouts combined.
985: - **Impact**: Every `youtube.feed` request silently failed. User saw "Loading feed..." for ~1s then "RPC request timed out." even though the plugin processed the request successfully. Only visible in WebView dev console (F12) — no terminal log.
986: - **Lesson**: Every RPC layer must have a timeout >= all the layers below it combined. Always set explicit `maxRequestTime` on EVERY `defineRPC()` call.
987: - **Related fixes applied**: readStdout buffer fix (already done), readStderr buffer fix (was still broken — same `lines.pop()` pattern), event queue with knownIds dedup (defeats Bun canary stdin re-delivery bug), feedLoadedRef guard (React double-mount protection)

1042: ## All Tools, Frameworks, and Concepts Discussed
1043: 
1044: ### Skeletons (App Frameworks)
1045: | Tool | Language | Approach | Bundle | Mobile | Stars | Notes |
1046: |------|----------|----------|--------|--------|-------|-------|
1047: | **Electrobun** | TypeScript (Bun) | System WebView | ~14MB | ❌ | Newer | Current choice for prototyping |
1048: | **Tauri** | Rust | System WebView | ~5-40MB | ✅ iOS+Android | ~107k | Future choice for production |
1049: | **zero-native** | Zig | System WebView | <1MB | ✅ iOS+Android | ~4.2k | Vercel Labs, pre-release v0.2 |
1050: | **WebUI (webui-dev)** | C | Opens real browser | Few KB | ❌ | ~4.1k | Interesting but no mobile |
1051: 
1052: ### Development Tools Suggested
1053: | Tool | Purpose | Why |
1054: |------|---------|-----|
1055: | **jq** | CLI JSON processor | Parse and format plugin JSON output during testing |
1056: | **watchexec** | File watcher | Auto-restart app when plugin source files change |
1057: | **hyperfine** | Benchmarking | Measure plugin response times |
1058: | **just / make** | Task runner | Replace long shell commands with named tasks |
1059: | **uv** | Python package manager | Faster than pip, useful for Python plugins |
1060: | **asdf / mise** | Version manager | Manage Go, Python, Rust versions per project |
1061: | **printf** | Shell command | Send JSON-RPC messages to plugin stdin for standalone testing |
1062: 
1063: ### Frontend Plugin Approaches
1064: | Approach | Isolation | Performance | Framework Lock-in | Communication |
1065: |----------|-----------|-------------|-------------------|---------------|
1066: | **Web Components** | Medium | Lightweight | None (standard) | Direct function calls |
1067: | **iframe** | High (separate JS context) | Heavier | None | postMessage async |
1068: | **Dynamic React import** | Low (same context) | Lightweight | React only | Direct imports |
1069: 
1070: ### iframe Details
1071: - Embeds a completely separate HTML document within the current page
1072: - Has its OWN JavaScript engine, its own DOM, its own CSS
1073: - CANNOT access or modify the host page's DOM (unless same-origin)
1074: - Communication only via `window.parent.postMessage()` and `window.addEventListener("message", ...)`
1075: - Can be sandboxed with `sandbox` attribute (restrict scripts, forms, popups, etc.)
1076: - Cannot display native UI (Qt, GTK, WinForms). Only HTML/CSS/JS
1077: - Each iframe consumes memory for a separate JS engine instance

1230: ## Teaching/Communication Rules (for agents working here)
1231: 
1232: ### The Two-File Rule (ABSOLUTE)
1233: 1. **MODIFY ONLY** `AGENTS.md` (project-specific knowledge) and `~/.config/opencode/skills/coding/SKILL.md` (general coding rules)
1234: 2. **NEVER TOUCH** any other project file — the user handles ALL code
1235: 3. **UPDATE BOTH FILES EVERY PROMPT** — actively check if anything changed. See the "Auto-Update Protocol" in SKILL.md.
1236: 4. **Always verify** — never assume "the last agent already updated this"
1237: 
1238: ### Teaching Style
1239: 1. **User is a beginner** — assume ZERO prior knowledge. Explain every concept, every syntax construct, every line
1240: 2. **Provide full code in messages** — user copies code themselves. Never modify files without explicit build mode permission
1241: 3. **Line-by-line explanation tables** — after every code block, explain each section in a table
1242: 4. **Multi-level zoom** — big picture → file → block → line → symbol → syntax construct
1243: 5. **Re-read files before every response** — stay in sync with what the user has written
1244: 6. **Research before speaking** — check latest docs for libraries, APIs, frameworks. Don't guess
1245: 7. **Surface better approaches** — if there's a better way, explain the tradeoffs and let the user decide
1246: 8. **Be proactive** — research and suggest relevant tools, patterns, and pitfalls without being asked
1247: 9. **Mentor, don't just answer** — correct wrong assumptions directly. Lead the project
1248: 10. **Test standalone before integrating** — always suggest testing plugins in isolation first
1249: 11. **No code comments unless asked** — don't add comments to source files
1250: 12. **Never commit unless asked** — no git operations without explicit instruction
1251: 13. **Never force push to main/master** — warn user if they request this
1252: 14. **Never amend unless the commit was just created by you and not pushed** — make a new commit for hook rejections

1274: ### Plugin Types
1275: - `backend` — only a subprocess, no UI contribution
1276: - `frontend` — only a Web Component, no subprocess
1277: - `fullstack` — both backend subprocess AND frontend Web Component

1284: 
1285: ## Phase 3 Architecture: Unified Feed
1286: 
1287: ### Core Shift
1288: Phase 1-2 built per-plugin standalone widgets (each plugin in its own card, rendered by App.tsx).
1289: Phase 3 replaces this with a SINGLE feed that aggregates items from all content plugins.
1290: 
1291: The feed itself is a plugin (`plugins/feed/`), swappable by the user. It has no backend — just a
1292: frontend Web Component (`feed-widget`). App.tsx loads manifests from the host, loads all frontend
1293: JS from `build/plugins/`, creates UI WC elements imperatively in a container div (passing manifests
1294: via `.manifests` setter). Feed-widget discovers feed-contributing plugins, calls their feed methods
1295: via `callHook()` or `__pluginRpc("name.method")`, and renders their card WCs.
1296: 
1297: Each content plugin provides:
1298: - **Backend**: RPC method that returns feed items (any shape)
1299: - **Frontend**: A Web Component "card" that renders ONE feed item
1300: - **Manifest**: Declares `feeds` array, `hooks` for capability discovery, `components` for WC tags
1301: 
1302: ### Architecture Diagram
1303: ```
1304: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1305: │  WebView (React + Tailwind + Vite HMR)                          │
1306: │                                                                  │
1307: │  App.tsx:                                                        │
1308: │  1. electroview.rpc.request.getPluginManifests({}) → manifests   │
1309: │  2. Collects WC tags: feeds[].card + ui → dedup                  │
1310: │  3. For each tag: loadFrontend("build/plugins/<tag>.js")         │
1311: │     (getPluginFrontend → <script> → customElements.define())     │
1312: │  4. Builds uiPlugins[] = manifests with ui field                 │
1313: │  5. For each ui plugin: createElement(tag), set .manifests,      │
1314: │     appendChild to #feed-container (imperative, not React)       │
1315: │         │                                                        │
1316: │         ▼                                                        │
1317: │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
1318: │  │ <feed-widget> (plugin: feed/)                        │        │
1319: │  │ set manifests(data) {                                │        │
1320: │  │   this._manifests = data;                            │        │
1321: │  │   this.loadFeed(); // trigger re-fetch               │        │
1322: │  │ }                                                    │        │
1323: │  │                                                      │        │
1324: │  │ loadFeed():                                          │        │
1325: │  │   1. Filter _manifests by has feeds[]                 │        │
1326: │  │   2. For each source:                                │        │
1327: │  │      a. __pluginRpc(name + "." + method, {})         │        │
1328: │  │      b. Receives items (any shape, no schema)         │        │
1329: │  │   3. Merges items (by source order)                   │        │
1330: │  │   4. For each item:                                   │        │
1331: │  │      cr = document.createElement(feeds[0].card)      │        │
1332: │  │      cr.item = rawItem (ALL data)                     │        │
1333: │  │      feedContainer.appendChild(cr)                   │        │
1334: │  │                                                      │        │
1335: │  │ States: loading|error|empty|partial|loaded           │        │
1336: │  │ Error banners with Sign In (searches all manifests   │        │
1337: │  │ for plugin with "login" method, not just source)     │        │
1338: │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
1339: │                                                                  │
1340: │  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐   │
1341: │  │ yt-video-card    │  │ peertube-card    │  │ player-modal │   │
1342: │  │ (from yt-card)   │  │ (from peertube)  │  │ (from vid-   │   │
1343: │  │ React 18         │  │ React 18         │  │  player)     │   │
1344: │  │ click→player-load│  │ click→player-load│  │ Listens for  │   │
1345: │  │ custom event     │  │ custom event     │  │ player-load  │   │
1346: │  └──────────────────┘  └──────────────────┘  └──────────────┘   │
1347: │                                                                  │
1348: │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
1349: │  │ player-modal (ui: "player-modal", created in #feed- │        │
1350: │  │ container by App.tsx alongside feed-widget)         │        │
1351: │  │ - Listens for "player-load" event on window        │        │
1352: │  │ - Opens iframe modal when event fires               │        │
1353: │  │ - Closes on Escape / click-outside / close button   │        │
1354: │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
1355: └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1356: ```
1357: 
1358: ### Data Flow (Detailed)
1359: 1. **App.tsx mounts** → `electroview.rpc.request.getPluginManifests({})` → gets array of all manifests
1360: 2. **App.tsx collects WC tags**: for each manifest, collects `feeds[*].card` and `ui` tags (dedup)
1361: 3. **App.tsx loads frontend JS**: for each unique tag:
1362:    - Calls `electroview.rpc.request.getPluginFrontend({ path: "build/plugins/<tag>.js" })`
1363:    - Creates `<script>` element, sets `textContent` = JS code, appends to `<body>`
1364:    - `customElements.define()` registers the WC globally
1365: 4. **App.tsx creates UI elements**: builds `uiPlugins[]` (manifests with `ui`), waits for each WC definition, creates element via `document.createElement(tag)`, sets `el.manifests = all`, appends to `#feed-container` div
1366: 5. **feed-widget receives manifests**: via `.manifests` setter (set by App.tsx's imperative code) → triggers `loadFeed()`
1367: 6. **feed-widget loads items**: for each source with `feeds[]`:
1368:    - Calls `__pluginRpc(source.name + "." + source.feeds[0].method, {})` (e.g., `"yt-feed.feed"`)
1369:    - Host splits method on first dot, finds plugin by `config.name`, routes to it
1370:    - Gets array of items (any JSON shape, no schema)
1371: 7. **Merges** items from all sources into one array (grouped by source, in registration order)
1372: 8. **For each item**: `customElements.whenDefined(source.feeds[0].card).then(() => {...})`
1373:    - `card = document.createElement(source.feeds[0].card)`
1374:    - `card.item = rawItem` (passes EVERYTHING — no schema)
1375:    - `feedContainer.appendChild(card)`
1376: 9. **Error handling**: per-source. If a feed method call fails, that source's items are skipped, an error banner is shown with optional "Sign in" button (searches ALL manifests for a plugin with `"login"` in methods, not just the errored source)
1377: 
1378: ### Key Design Decisions
1379: - **No schema**: Feed doesn't know or care about item structure. Raw data passed through to card WC.
1380: - **Feed is a plugin**: Swappable. Lives at `plugins/feed/` with no backend.
1381: - **Framework agnostic**: Each card WC is a self-contained IIFE with framework inlined.
1382: - **Language agnostic**: Backend plugins can be any language.
1383: - **No fallback cards**: Cards must come from plugins. Items without cards are skipped. Postponed.
1384: - **Path derivation**: Frontend file paths NOT in manifest. Loaded from `build/plugins/<tag>.js`.
1385:   Build script finds source by `<pluginDir>/<tag>.<ext>`. No `frontend/` subdirectory.
1386: - **Custom DOM events for card ↔ modal communication**: Cards dispatch `CustomEvent("player-load", {detail: {url, title}})` on `window`. Player-modal listens via `addEventListener`.
1387: - **`name + "." + method` RPC prefix**: Host routes by finding plugin with `config.name === firstPart`. Enables simple method names ("feed", "list") without namespace pollution.
1388: 
1389: ### Simplified Plugin Manifest (Phase 3 — Current)
1390: 
1391: ```json
1392: {
1393:   "name": "yt-feed",
1394:   "run": "bun plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/main.ts",
1395:   "hooks": ["feed.video"],
1396:   "methods": ["feed"],
1397:   "feeds": [{ "type": "video", "card": "yt-video-card" }]
1398: }
1399: ```
1400: 
1401: | Field | Required | Description |
1402: |-------|----------|-------------|
1403: | `name` | ✅ | Unique plugin ID |
1404: | `run` | ❌ | Command to spawn subprocess. |
1405: | `methods` | ❌ | Array of method names. Method called as `name + "." + method` (e.g., `"yt-feed.feed"`). |
1406: | `hooks` | ❌ | Array of hook strings for capability discovery (e.g., `"feed.video"`, `"auth"`). |
1407: | `version` | ❌ | Semver version. |
1408: | `description` | ❌ | Short description. |
1409: | `author` | ❌ | Creator name. |
1410: | `ui` | ❌ | WC tag for main-UI WC. Loaded from `build/plugins/<tag>.js`. Mounted by App.tsx. |
1411: | `components` | ❌ | Array of WC tags to build but NOT mount. Example: `["yt-video-card"]`. |
1412: | `feeds` | ❌ | Array of feed contribution objects. |
1413: | `feeds[].type` | ✅ (if feeds) | Content type: `"video"`, `"image"`, `"post"`, `"short"`, etc. |
1414: | `feeds[].method` | ❌ | RPC method to call. Defaults to `methods[0]`. |
1415: | `feeds[].card` | ❌ | WC tag for rendering one item. Loaded from `build/plugins/<tag>.js`.
1416: 
1417: ### `ui` field meaning (Phase 3)
1418: In Phase 1-2, `ui` meant a standalone widget card rendered by App.tsx. In Phase 3, `ui` simply means
1419: "this plugin has a frontend WC that App.tsx should load AND mount." The frontend file is loaded from
1420: `build/plugins/<tag>.js`. The `feed` plugin uses `ui: "feed-widget"`. The `video-player` plugin uses
1421: `ui: "player-modal"`. App.tsx creates WC elements for ALL ui plugins, not just the last one.
1422: 
1423: ### Backward Compatibility
1424: - Old format (`command`+`args`, `frontendComponent`, `frontendSlot`) is phased out completely.
1425: - Host reads ONLY new format. Old prototype plugins removed from disk.
1426: - Phase 1/2 demo plugins (greet-go, logger-py, joke-fetcher, youtube-explorer) removed entirely.
1427: 
1428: ### The `feed` Plugin
1429: 
1430: ```
1431: plugins/feed/
1432: ├── plugin.json         → { name: "feed", ui: "feed-widget" }
1433: └── feed-widget.tsx      ← orchestrator WC (React via build system, no frontend/ subdir)
1434: ```
1435: 
1436: `plugin.json`:
1437: ```json
1438: {
1439:   "name": "feed",
1440:   "description": "Aggregate content from all your plugins into a single feed",
1441:   "author": "Me",
1442:   "version": "1.0.0",
1443:   "ui": "feed-widget"
1444: }
1445: ```
1446: 
1447: - No `run` — no backend process needed
1448: - No `feeds` — it IS the feed, not a contributor
1449: - `ui: "feed-widget"` — App.tsx loads `build/plugins/feed-widget.js` and creates `<feed-widget>` in `#feed-container`
1450: 
1451: ### __pluginRpc Bridge (Phase 3 — Simple, No host.*)
1452: 
1453: The `__pluginRpc` bridge stays simple: it only routes to plugin subprocesses. No `host.*` prefix.
1454: 
1455: ```javascript
1456: window.__pluginRpc = async (method, params) => {
1457:   const res = await electroview.rpc?.request.pluginRequest({ method, params })
1458:   if (!res.success) throw new Error(res.error || "RPC error")
1459:   return res.data
1460: }
1461: ```
1462: 
1463: App.tsx calls host RPCs directly via `electroview.rpc.request.getPluginManifests({})` and
1464: `electroview.rpc.request.getPluginFrontend({ path })` — NOT through `__pluginRpc`.
1465: 
1466: **Why no `host.*`?** The feed-widget doesn't need to call host RPCs. App.tsx (which has
1467: `electroview` in scope) calls the host directly and passes data to feed-widget via
1468: the `.manifests` property setter. This keeps `__pluginRpc` simple (one routing path)
1469: and avoids adding host routing logic to the bridge.
1470: 
1471: ### Per-Instance Framework Sharing (No Action Needed)
1472: When the feed has 20 `<yt-video-card>` elements, they all share ONE WC class definition.
1473: The framework (React, etc.) is in the class prototype, not in each DOM element.
1474: `customElements.define("yt-video-card", YTVideoCard)` registers one class.
1475: Each `<yt-video-card>` is just an instance — they share the prototype.
1476: **No build-time sharing optimization needed. Ever.**
1477: 
1478: ### Frontend Path Derivation
1479: 
1480: | Manifest field | Purpose | Build source | Runtime load path |
1481: |----------------|---------|-------------|-------------------|
1482: | `ui: "feed-widget"` | Main UI WC to mount | `plugins/feed/feed-widget.tsx` | `build/plugins/feed-widget.js` |
1483: | `components: ["yt-video-card"]` | WC to build only | `plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-card/yt-video-card.tsx` | `build/plugins/yt-video-card.js` |
1484: | `feeds[i].card: "yt-video-card"` | Card WC for register | (same as components — see above) | `build/plugins/yt-video-card.js` |
1485: 
1486: Build script searches for source: `<pluginDir>/<tag>.<ext>` where ext is tsx, jsx, vue, svelte.
1487: Cross-directory: if not found in declaring plugin's dir, it must be declared in another plugin's `components` or `ui`.
1488: 
1489: ### Card WC Contract
1490: 
1491: The feed passes data to card WCs via a `.item` property setter. All WCs also get `.manifests`.
1492: Each card WC is a Web Component wrapping a React/Preact component.
1493: 
1494: #### The Pattern (React entry template — current)
1495: 
1496: Build script generates this `entry.tsx` for every React frontend:
1497: 
1498: ```javascript
1499: import Component from "./yt-video-card.tsx"
1500: import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client"
1501: customElements.define("yt-video-card", class extends HTMLElement {
1502:   root = null
1503:   _item = null
1504:   _manifests = null
1505:   connectedCallback() {
1506:     try { this.root = createRoot(this); this._render() }
1507:     catch (e) { this.innerHTML = `<p style="color:red">WC error: ${e}</p>` }
1508:   }
1509:   disconnectedCallback() { this.root?.unmount(); this.root = null }
1510:   set item(d) { this._item = d; this._render() }
1511:   set manifests(d) { this._manifests = d; this._render() }
1512:   _render() {
1513:     if (!this.root) return
1514:     this.root.render(<Component item={this._item} manifests={this._manifests} />)
1515:   }
1516: })
1517: ```
1518: 
1519: #### Data Flow (One Item)
1520: 
1521: 1. Feed calls `__pluginRpc("yt-feed.feed", {})` → gets array of items
1522: 2. Feed loops: `for (const item of items)`
1523: 3. `document.createElement("yt-video-card")` → browser creates WC → `connectedCallback()` runs
1524:    - React mount: `createRoot(this)` → `_render()` → `<Component item={null} />` → shows "Loading..."
1525: 4. `card.item = item` → setter fires:
1526:    - `this._item = item` — stores the data
1527:    - `this._render()` — `root.render(<Component item={{ title: "Cats", ... }} />)`
1528:    - React re-renders component with real data → shows title, thumbnail, etc.
1529: 5. `feedContainer.appendChild(card)` — adds to page display
1530: 
1531: API calls = number of PLUGINS (not items). One `"yt-feed.feed"` call returns N items → N cards.
1532: 
1533: #### Why `_item` (underscore)?
1534: 
1535: A setter cannot store data in a variable with the same name (`item`), because `this.item = data`
1536: inside a `set item()` would call itself forever (infinite loop). So we separate:
1537: 
1538: | Name | Role | Type |
1539: |------|------|------|
1540: | `item` (setter) | PUBLIC — called by feed | Function (runs on `=`) |
1541: | `_item` | PRIVATE storage | Regular variable (no setter) |
1542: | `item` (getter) | PUBLIC — read by feed | Function (runs on read) |
1543: 
1544: The underscore `_` is a naming convention meaning "internal, don't touch directly."
1545: 
1546: #### Entry Templates
1547: 
1548: All frameworks (React, Preact, Vue, Svelte) get entry templates with both `_item` and `_manifests`
1549: setters. The template is auto-generated by the build script based on detected framework.
1550: 
1551: #### Build Script Tag Resolution (FIXED)
1552: 
1553: The build script now correctly checks `manifest.ui`, `manifest.components[]`, and
1554: `manifest.feeds[*].card` to discover WC tags. Old `frontendComponent` field is not checked.
1555: If a tag is referenced (e.g., `feeds[0].card: "yt-video-card"`) but source not found in that
1556: plugin's directory, the build script skips it. The tag WILL be built if another plugin declares
1557: it in `components[]` (yt-card does: `components: ["yt-video-card"]`).
1558: 
1559: Design: **Declarative ownership via `components`** — each plugin declares what WCs it owns.
1560: The build script doesn't cross-search. If a plugin references a card from another plugin,
1561: the source is found only in the owning plugin's directory.
1562: 
1563: ### Phase 3 Implementation — DONE (Extended)
1564: 
1565: Phase 3 core was completed earlier. This session extended it with:
1566: - **`components` field** — separates "build this WC" from "mount this WC"
1567: - **`hooks` field** — decentralized capability discovery instead of hardcoded routing
1568: - **`feeds` as array** — a single plugin can contribute to multiple feed types
1569: - **Plugin nesting** — plugins under `plugins/youtube/plugins/*/` for logical grouping
1570: - **`name + "." + method` routing** — host splits on first dot, routes by plugin name
1571: - **Monolithic plugin split** — youtube-explorer → yt-feed, yt-auth, yt-search, yt-card
1572: - **Multiple UI plugins** — App.tsx mounts ALL plugins with `ui`, not just the last one
1573: - **Locked auth resolution** — sign-in button searches ALL manifests, not just errored source
1574: - **Lazy cookie reload** — yt-feed re-reads cookie at request time, not startup
1575: - **Custom event bridge** — cards dispatch `player-load` event, player-modal listens
1576: - **Iframe-based player** — `<iframe>` instead of `<video>` for embed URLs
1577: - **Vite-based build** — all frameworks via Vite IIFE, auto-detect by import scanning

293: 40: Current working state: Feed-widget displays all 5 render states (loading, auth-required,
294: 41: error per source, empty, cards). yt-feed (YouTube feed via Innertube API) works with
295: 42: lazy cookie reload. yt-auth plugin provides login/logout/status using browser DB discovery
296: 43: and writes shared cookie file. yt-card provides `yt-video-card` as a `components` entry
297: 44: (not `ui` — never mounted as top-level view, only instantiated per feed item). Player modal
298: 45: uses iframe and `player-load` custom event. peertube-card and peertube-feed are functional
299: 46: for PeerTube. Sign-in buttons per auth plugin are shown/hidden based on searching ALL
300: 47: manifests for a plugin with `methods.includes("login")`.
301: 48: 
302: 49: ---
303: 50: 
304: 51: ## Goal
305: 52: Build a language-agnostic, fully modular desktop app where every feature is a plugin.
306: 53: The plugin system is independent of the "skeleton" (the app framework). The same plugins
307: 54: work on any skeleton — Electrobun (desktop now), Tauri or zero-native (desktop + mobile later).
308: 55: 
309: 56: Long-term vision: a unified API client that aggregates every internet service into one
310: 57: interface. Content is categorized by MEDIA TYPE (posts, shorts, videos, images, DMs, etc.),
311: 58: not by service. Users get one feed per media type populated from all the services they
312: 59: choose. Features are generalized per media type — if someone builds auto-scroll for shorts,
313: 60: ALL shorts (TikTok, Reels, YT Shorts) get it automatically. This will be built GRADUALLY,
314: 61: starting with one simple API at a time.
315: 62: 
316: 63: ---
317: 64: 
318: 65: ## Long-Term Vision — Unified API Client
319: 66: 
320: 67: ### The Problem
321: 68: Currently every internet service has its own dedicated client app:
322: 69: - NewPipe for YouTube, Alicord for Discord
323: 70: - Separate apps for Twitter, Instagram, Telegram, Reddit, TikTok
324: 71: - Different UI, different features, different codebases — no sharing between them
325: 72: 
326: 73: ### The Solution: One App for Every API
327: 74: A single desktop app where every internet service is a plugin.
328: 75: Content is organized by MEDIA TYPE, not by service.
329: 76: 
330: 77: **Media Type Examples**
331: 78: - **Posts/Threads**: Reddit posts, Twitter threads, Bluesky, Hacker News stories
332: 79: - **Shorts**: TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, Reddit Watch
333: 80: - **Long Videos**: YouTube, PeerTube, Vimeo, Nebula
334: 81: - **Images**: Instagram, Flickr, Imgur, 500px
335: 82: - **DMs/Chat**: Discord DMs, Telegram, Twitter DMs, Instagram DMs
336: 83: - **Live**: Twitch, YouTube Live, Kick
337: 84: - **Music**: Spotify, YouTube Music, SoundCloud
338: 85: - **Books**: Goodreads, Project Gutenberg, Archive.org
339: 86: - **Shopping**: Amazon, eBay, Etsy — unified product feed
340: 87: - **Anime/Manga**: MyAnimeList, AniList, Crunchyroll, MangaDex
341: 88: - **Recipes**: AllRecipes, SeriousEats, NYT Cooking
342: 89: - ...and anything else — theoretically infinite (one per API endpoint type)
343: 90: 
344: 91: Each media type has one feed in the app. The user adds/removes services from each
345: 92: feed freely. Adding a new service to a feed gives you ALL that service's content
346: 93: mixed in with everything else.
347: 94: 
348: 95: ### Generalized Features per Media Type
349: 96: Features attach to the MEDIA TYPE, not the service:
350: 97: - Auto-scroll for shorts feed → ALL shorts get it (TikTok + Reels + YT Shorts)
351: 98: - Ad-skip for long videos → ALL long videos get it
352: 99: - Download for images → ALL images from any service get it
353: 100: - Translation for posts → ALL posts get it
354: 101: - Any QoL feature built by the community → works everywhere instantly
355: 102: 
356: 103: No more waiting for YouTube to add a feature you want. No more missing auto-scroll
357: 104: on Reels while TikTok has it. The community builds features once, and they work for
358: 105: every service with that media type.
359: 106: 
360: 107: ### How We Get There (Gradual)
361: 108: 1. Start with simple individual API plugins (fetch data, show on screen)
362: 109: 2. When multiple plugins produce the same media type → build a unified feed
363: 110: 3. Build generalized features for that media type
364: 111: 4. Repeat for more APIs and media types as interest grows
365: 112: 5. Architecture evolves organically as patterns emerge (no premature abstraction)
366: 113: 
367: 114: **This is a long-term vision, not a right-now requirement. We're prototyping:
368: 115: building the first real API plugin to fetch internet data and show it on screen.**
369: 116:

372: 119: ## Core Architecture
373: 120: 
374: 121: ### Current Architecture (Phase 1 Complete)
375: 122: 
376: 123: ```
377: 124: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
378: 125: │  WebView (React + Tailwind + Vite HMR)                           │
379: 126: │  App.tsx (~152 lines):                                           │
380: 127: │  - Loads all manifests on mount                                  │
381: 128: │  - Auto-loads all plugin Web Components via <script> injection   │
382: 129: │  - Plugin cards with alive/dead badge + method buttons           │
383: 130: │  - WebComponentSlot renders each plugin's WC directly in card    │
384: 131: │  - Result display (formatted JSON)                                │
385: 132: │         │                                                        │
386: 133: │         │ window.__pluginRpc(method, params)                     │
387: 134: │         │     → electroview.rpc.request.pluginRequest()          │
388: 135: │         ▼                                                        │
389: 136: │  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
390: 137: │  │ Host (Bun process — src/bun/index.ts ~272 lines)           │  │
391: 138: │  │ 1. findProjectRoot() — walks up from import.meta.dir       │  │
392: 139: │  │ 2. Scans plugins/*/plugin.json via readdirSync + JSON.parse│  │
393: 140: │  │ 3. resolvePath() — makes relative paths absolute for spawn │  │
394: 141: │  │ 4. Spawns plugins via Bun.spawn() (stdin/stdout pipes)     │  │
395: 142: │  │ 5. sendToPlugin() — writes JSON to plugin stdin            │  │
396: 143: │  │ 6. readStdout() — async reader with line buffering         │  │
397: 144: │  │ 7. routeRequest() — method prefix match → Promise(10s)     │  │
398: 145: │  │ 8. 4 RPC handlers: pluginRequest, pluginList,              │  │
399: 146: │  │    getPluginManifests, getPluginFrontend                    │  │
400: 147: │  │ 9. Health check (5s), SIGINT cleanup                       │  │
401: 148: │  └──┬────────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────┘  │
402: 149: │     │ stdin/stdout   │ stdin/stdout                              │
403: 150: │  ┌──▼──────────┐  ┌─▼────────────┐                              │
404: 151: │  │ Go Plugin    │  │ Python       │                              │
405: 152: │  │ (greet)      │  │ Plugin       │                              │
406: 153: │  │ greet.hello  │  │ (logger)     │                              │
407: 154: │  │ greet.bye    │  │ log.info     │                              │
408: 155: │  │              │  │ log.list     │                              │
409: 156: │  └──────────────┘  └──────────────┘                              │
410: 157: │                                                                  │
411: 158: │  Frontend Plugins (Web Components, injected into WebView):       │
412: 159: │  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐                     │
413: 160: │  │ <greet-widget>    │  │ <log-viewer>     │                     │
414: 161: │  │ (Preact, esbuild) │  │ (Vue, Vite build)│                     │
415: 162: │  │ Hello/Bye buttons │  │ Refresh + log    │                     │
416: 163: │  │ JSON result       │  │ list display     │                     │
417: 164: │  └──────────────────┘  └──────────────────┘                     │
418: 165: └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
419: 166: ```
420: 167: 
421: 168: ### Data Flow (End-to-End — Phase 3)
422: 169: 1. App starts → Host spawns all backend plugins with `run` field via recursive manifest scan
423: 170: 2. WebView loads → App.tsx mounts (Electroview RPC bridge initialized)
424: 171: 3. App.tsx calls `getPluginManifests` → gets array of all manifests
425: 172: 4. App.tsx collects WC tags from `feeds[*].card` and `ui` fields (dedup)
426: 173: 5. For each unique tag:
427: 174:    - Call `getPluginFrontend({ path: "build/plugins/<tag>.js" })` → returns JS as string
428: 175:    - Create `<script>` element, set `textContent` = code, append to `<body>`
429: 176:    - Script calls `customElements.define()` → Web Component registered globally
430: 177: 6. App.tsx builds `uiPlugins[]` array, creates each UI WC imperatively via `document.createElement` in `#feed-container`, sets `.manifests = all`
431: 178: 7. Feed-widget (one of the UI WCs) receives manifests via `.manifests` setter, calls `loadFeed()`
432: 179: 8. Feed-widget discovers feed sources (plugins with `feeds[]`), calls `__pluginRpc(name + "." + method, {})` for each
433: 180: 9. Host `routeRequest` splits method on first dot → finds plugin by `config.name` → sends action to plugin stdin
434: 181: 10. Plugin reads stdin line, processes request (e.g., Innertube API call), writes response to stdout
435: 182: 11. Host reads stdout line, parses JSON, matches by `id`, resolves promise
436: 183: 12. Result flows back through RPC → `window.__pluginRpc` returns → feed-widget receives items
437: 184: 13. Feed-widget creates card WCs (`document.createElement(tag)`), sets `.item = rawItem`, appends to container
438: 185:
