581: 328: ## Plugin Protocol (Detailed)
582: 329: 
583: 330: ### Message Format
584: 331: ```json
585: 332: {"id": 1, "method": "greet.hello", "params": {"name": "Niri"}}
586: 333: ```
587: 334: - `id`: number — unique per request, matched in response
588: 335: - `method`: string — format is `namespace.action` (e.g., `greet.hello`, `log.info`)
589: 336: - `params`: optional object — any JSON structure the plugin expects
590: 337: - NO `jsonrpc` field (simplified from JSON-RPC spec)
591: 338: 
592: 339: ### Response Format
593: 340: ```json
594: 341: {"id": 1, "result": {"message": "Hello Niri from Go!"}}
595: 342: ```
596: 343: - On success: `{"id": <same id>, "result": <any>}`
597: 344: - On error:   `{"id": <same id>, "error": "<message>"}`
598: 345: - Messages are newline-delimited: one JSON object per line (`\n`)
599: 346: 
600: 347: ### Protocol Rules
601: 348: 1. Plugin reads exactly one line from stdin
602: 349: 2. Plugin processes the request
603: 350: 3. Plugin writes exactly one line to stdout
604: 351: 4. Plugins MUST flush stdout after writing (`fmt.Println` in Go auto-flushes; Python needs `sys.stdout.flush()`)
605: 352: 5. Host matches response to pending request by `id`
606: 353: 6. If no response within 10 seconds, the Promise rejects with timeout error
607: 354: 7. No connection keepalive, no persistent state between requests (each request is stateless)
608: 355: 
609: 356: ### Host Routing Logic
610: 357: ```typescript
611: 358: for (const plugin of plugins) {
612: 359:     if (!plugin.alive) continue
613: 360:     for (const ns of plugin.config.methods) {
614: 361:         if (method.startsWith(ns)) {
615: 362:             // Route to this plugin
616: 363:         }
617: 364:     }
618: 365: }
619: 366: ```
620: 367: - Host checks method PREFIX only (e.g., `"greet."` matches `"greet.hello"` and `"greet.bye"`)
621: 368: - The specific action (hello vs bye) is handled by the plugin, NOT the host
622: 369: - Adding 100+ plugins requires zero changes to routing code
623: 370: - Order matters: first matching plugin in the manifests array wins
624: 371: 
625: 372: ---
626: 373: 
627: 374: ## Host Behavior (src/bun/index.ts — ~340 lines)
628: 375: 
629: 376: ### Startup Sequence
630: 377: 1. `findProjectRoot(import.meta.dir)` — walks up directory tree until `package.json` found. Works in both dev and bundled modes.
631: 378: 2. `baseDir = findProjectRoot(...)` — store the project root absolute path
632: 379: 3. `getAllPluginManifests(join(baseDir, "plugins"))` — recursive directory scan: for each dir with `plugin.json`, parse JSON; recurse into subdirectories. Supports nested plugins (e.g., `plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/`).
633: 380: 4. For each manifest with `run` field (formerly `"command"`):
634: 381:    a. Split `run` by whitespace → `[cmd, ...args]` (single string for command + args)
635: 382:    b. `resolvePath(cmd)` and `resolvePath(args)` — if relative, join with baseDir; absolute as-is; bare name (bun/python3) returned unmodified
636: 383:    c. `Bun.spawn([cmd, ...args], { stdin: "pipe", stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" })`
637: 384:    d. Store as `PluginInstance { config: manifest, process: proc, alive: true }`
638: 385:    e. Start async `readStdout(plugin)` + `readStderr(plugin)`
639: 386:    f. `proc.exited.then(code => { plugin.alive = false })` — marks dead on exit
640: 387: 5. Define RPC handlers via `BrowserView.defineRPC()` — 6 request handlers (see RPC table)
641: 388: 6. If bundled mode (no Vite): start static server via `startStaticServer()` -> `Bun.serve()` that serves `dist/` or `views/mainview/`
642: 389: 7. `getMainViewUrl()` — checks Vite HMR on port 5173 (in dev channel), returns dev URL if available, else bundled HTML via static server
643: 390: 8. `new BrowserWindow({ title, url, frame, rpc })` — create the app window
644: 391: 9. `setInterval()` — health check every 5 seconds (logs dead plugins, no auto-restart)
645: 392: 10. `process.on("SIGINT")` — stop server, kill all plugin processes, exit
646: 393: 
647: 394: ### RPC Handlers
648: 395: 
649: 396: All handlers use `(params: unknown) =>` with internal casts.
650: 397: 
651: 398: | Handler | Params (cast from unknown) | Returns |
652: 399: |---------|---------------------------|---------|
653: 400: | `pluginRequest` | `{ method: string, params: any }` | `{ success, data?, error? }` |
654: 401: | `pluginList` | ignored | `[{ name, alive, methods }]` |
655: 402: | `getPluginManifests` | ignored | `[{ name, version?, description?, author?, methods[], hooks[], ui?, feeds? }]` |
656: 403: | `getPluginFrontend` | `{ path: string }` | `{ code: string }` or `{ error: string }` |
657: 404: | `resolveHook` | `{ hook: string }` | `{ success, data: { name, methods } }` or `{ success: false, error }` |
658: 405: | `callHook` | `{ hook: string, method?: string, params: any }` | `{ success, data? }` or `{ success: false, error }` |
659: 406: 
660: 407: **RPC details:**
661: 408: - `pluginRequest(method, params)`: calls `routeRequest(method, params)` which splits method by `.` — first part is plugin name, rest is action. Finds plugin by `config.name`, sends `{id, method: action, params}` via stdin. Returns Promise with 10s timeout.
662: 409: - `getPluginManifests`: returns all manifests with fields: name, version, description, author, methods, hooks, ui, feeds. No `components` field returned (yet — yt-card still identified for frontend loading by App.tsx scanning feeds[].card + ui).
663: 410: - `getPluginFrontend({ path })`: restricted to `build/plugins/` directory (security). Reads file via `Bun.file().text()`.
664: 411: - `resolveHook({ hook })`: finds first plugin with `config.hooks.includes(hook)`. Returns `{name, methods}`.
665: 412: - `callHook({ hook, method?, params })`: finds plugin for hook, calls `routeRequest(name.method, params)`. Defaults to `methods[0]` if no method specified.
666: 413: 
667: 414: ### stdout Reader (readStdout)
668: 415: - Web Streams API: `plugin.process.stdout.getReader()`
669: 416: - Buffers partial lines across chunks (split by `\n`, keep incomplete line in buffer via `lines.pop()`)
670: 417: - Each complete line passed to `handlePluginResponse()`
671: 418: 
672: 419: ### Response Handling (handlePluginResponse)
673: 420: 1. `JSON.parse(line)` → get `msg`
674: 421: 2. Match by `msg.id` to pending request
675: 422: 3. `clearTimeout(timer)` + `pendingRequests.delete(id)`
676: 423: 4. `msg.error` exists → `reject(new Error(msg.error))`
677: 424: 5. Else → `resolve(msg.result)`
678: 425: 
679: 426: ### Health Check
680: 427: - `setInterval()` every 5000ms
681: 428: - Logs dead plugins (no auto-restart)
682: 429: 
683: 430: ### Cleanup
684: 431: - `process.on("SIGINT")` — kills all plugin subprocesses, stops static server
685: 432: 
686: 433: ---
687: 434: 
688: 435: ## Frontend Behavior (src/mainview/App.tsx — ~102 lines)
689: 436: 
690: 437: ### Imports & Setup
691: 438: - `useState, useEffect` from React
692: 439: - `Electroview` from electrobun/view (Electrobun's browser-side RPC bridge)
693: 440: - Type imports: `PluginManifest` from shared/types
694: 441: - NO `useRef` — UI plugin elements created imperatively, not via React refs
695: 442: 
696: 443: ### RPC Configuration
697: 444: ```typescript
698: 445: const electroview = new Electroview({
699: 446:   rpc: Electroview.defineRPC({
700: 447:     maxRequestTime: 20000,  // MUST be >= all inner timeouts combined
701: 448:     handlers: { requests: {}, messages: {} },
702: 449:   }),
703: 450: })
704: 451: ```
705: 452: - `maxRequestTime: 20000` is CRITICAL. Host has 15000ms, routeRequest has 10s, plugin has 8s.
706: 453:   Frontend timeout must be the largest (20s) because it's the outermost caller.
707: 454: 
708: 455: ### Global Bridges (module-level, outside App component)
709: 456: ```typescript
710: 457: window.__pluginRpc = async (method: string, params: any) => {
711: 458:   const res = await electroview.rpc?.request.pluginRequest({ method, params })
712: 459:   if (!res.success) throw new Error(res.error || "RPC error")
713: 460:   return res.data
714: 461: }
715: 462: ```
716: 463: - Any WC can call `window.__pluginRpc(method, params)` without importing Electrobun
717: 464: - No `host.*` routing — bridge only routes to plugin subprocesses
718: 465: - Method format: `"name.action"` (e.g., `"yt-feed.feed"`) — host splits on first dot to find plugin by name
719: 466: 
720: 467: ```typescript
721: 468: window.resolveHook = async (hook: string) => {
722: 469:   const res = await electroview.rpc.request.resolveHook({ hook })
723: 470:   if (!res.success) throw new Error(res.error || "Hook resolution failed")
724: 471:   return res.data
725: 472: }
726: 473: window.callHook = async (hook: string, methodOrArgs: any, args?: any) => {
727: 474:   const method = args !== undefined ? methodOrArgs : undefined
728: 475:   const params = args !== undefined ? args : methodOrArgs
729: 476:   const res = await electroview.rpc.request.callHook({ hook, method, params })
730: 477:   if (!res.success) throw new Error(res.error || "callHook failed")
731: 478:   return res.data
732: 479: }
733: 480: ```
734: 481: - `resolveHook(hook)` → finds plugin providing that hook (e.g., `"feed.video"` → yt-feed)
735: 482: - `callHook(hook, method?, args)` → resolves hook + calls plugin method
736: 483: 
737: 484: ### App Component — State
738: 485: - `manifests` — array of `PluginManifest` from `getPluginManifests` RPC
739: 486: 
740: 487: ### On Mount — Init Function
741: 488: ```typescript
742: 489: useEffect(() => { init().catch(e => { ... }) }, [])
743: 490: ```
744: 491: `init()` does:
745: 492: 1. Fetches manifests via `electroview.rpc.request.getPluginManifests({})`
746: 493: 2. For each manifest, collects WC tags from `feeds[].card` and `ui` (dedup by tag)
747: 494: 3. Loads each frontend JS via `getPluginFrontend({ path: "build/plugins/<tag>.js" })`
748: 495:    - `path` starts with `build/plugins/` (NOT `plugins/x/frontend/y.js`)
749: 496:    - Restricted to `build/plugins/` directory by host security check
750: 497: 4. Builds `uiPlugins[]` array — all manifests with `ui` field
751: 498: 5. For each UI plugin: waits for WC definition, creates element imperatively, sets `.manifests = all`, appends to `#feed-container`
752: 499:    - Creates elements for ALL UI plugins (not just last one)
753: 500:    - Uses `document.getElementById("feed-container")` — not React refs
754: 501: 
755: 502: ### Render
756: 503: ```typescript
757: 504: return (
758: 505:   <div className="...">
759: 506:     <h1>Electro Plugins</h1>
760: 507:     <div id="feed-container" />
761: 508:   </div>
762: 509: )
763: 510: ```
764: 511: - Only renders a container div — UI plugin elements are created imperatively inside it
765: 512: - No React refs to web components — elements managed via `document.getElementById`
766: 513: - No `<feed-widget>` in JSX — created imperatively
767: 514: 
768: 515: ---
769: 516: 
770: 517: ## Build System
771: 518: 
772: 519: `scripts/build-plugins.ts` (~191 lines) — centralized build for all plugin frontends.
773: 520: 
774: 521: ### How It Works
775: 522: 1. Scans `plugins/` recursively via `findPluginDirs()` — finds all directories containing `plugin.json` (supports nested plugins like `plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-card/`)
776: 523: 2. For each plugin dir, reads `plugin.json` and collects WC tag names from:
777: 524:    - `manifest.ui` (single tag, e.g., `"feed-widget"`)
778: 525:    - `manifest.components[]` (array of tags, e.g., `["yt-video-card"]`)
779: 526:    - `manifest.feeds[*].card` (card tags from each feed contribution, e.g., `"yt-video-card"`)
780: 527: 3. Deduplicates tags across plugins (`new Set()`)
781: 528: 4. For each unique tag:
782: 529:    a. Finds source file: checks `<dir>/<tag>.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.vue`, `.svelte` in order
783: 530:    b. If not found in plugin's dir, skips (defers to plugin that declares it — cross-directory ownership via `components` field)
784: 531:    c. Reads source content to auto-detect framework (React vs Preact) via import string matching
785: 532:    d. Generates a temporary `.vite.config.mjs`, `entry.tsx` (with WC boilerplate), and `style.css`
786: 533:    e. Runs `bunx vite build --config <configFile>` targeting IIFE format
787: 534:    f. Output: `build/plugins/<tag>.js` (deleted temp files after build)
788: 535: 5. Framework auto-detection: reads source file, checks for `"react"`/`"react-dom"` imports (React) vs `"preact"`/`"preact/hooks"` (Preact). Falls back to first match if ambiguous.
789: 536: 
790: 537: ### Entry Template (React example)
791: 538: Generated by the build script's `entry()` function:
792: 539: ```typescript
793: 540: import Component from "./yt-video-card.tsx"
794: 541: import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client"
795: 542: customElements.define("yt-video-card", class extends HTMLElement {
796: 543:   root = null
797: 544:   _item = null
798: 545:   _manifests = null
799: 546:   connectedCallback() { this.root = createRoot(this); this._render() }
800: 547:   disconnectedCallback() { this.root?.unmount(); this.root = null }
801: 548:   set item(d) { this._item = d; this._render() }
802: 549:   set manifests(d) { this._manifests = d; this._render() }
803: 550:   _render() { this.root.render(<Component item={this._item} manifests={this._manifests} />) }
804: 551: })
805: 552: ```
806: 553: - All WCs get `_item` and `_manifests` setters (even non-card WCs — harmless)
807: 554: - CSS inlined via `vite-plugin-css-injected-by-js` (Tailwind classes included)
808: 555: 
809: 556: ### Tag Sources
810: 557: | Manifest Field | Type | Purpose |
811: 558: |---------------|------|---------|
812: 559: | `ui: "feed-widget"` | string | Main UI WC (built + mounted by App.tsx) |
813: 560: | `components: ["yt-video-card"]` | string[] | Built-only WCs (not mounted by App.tsx) |
814: 561: | `feeds[i].card: "yt-video-card"` | string | Feed item card WCs (loaded, mounted by feed-widget) |
815: 562: 
816: 563: ### Cross-Directory Source Discovery
817: 564: When a plugin references a WC tag (via `feeds[].card`) but the source file isn't in that plugin's directory:
818: 565: - Build script logs `skip <tag> (source not found in <dir>)`
819: 566: - The tag WILL be built if ANOTHER plugin declares it in `components[]` or `ui`
820: 567: - Fix: Declare `components: ["<tag>"]` on the plugin that owns the source file
821: 568: - Example: `plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-card/plugin.json` has `components: ["yt-video-card"]` — builds the source in its own directory
822: 569: 
823: 570: ### Entry Template Paths (at runtime, in App.tsx)
824: 571: Frontend JS is loaded from `build/plugins/<tag>.js` via `getPluginFrontend({ path })`.
825: 572: Previously: `plugins/<name>/frontend/<tag>.js`. Now: `build/plugins/<tag>.js`.
826: 573: 
827: 574: ### Run Commands
828: 575: ```bash
829: 576: bun run build:plugins          # Build all plugin frontends (output to build/plugins/)
830: 577: bun run start                  # build:plugins + vite build + electrobun dev
831: 578: ```
832: 579: 
833: 580: ### Framework Handling
834: 581: | Framework | Source Ext | Build Tool | Bundle Size |
835: 582: |-----------|-----------|------------|-------------|
836: 583: | React | .tsx/.jsx | Vite (IIFE) | ~40KB + code |
837: 584: | Preact | .tsx/.jsx | Vite (IIFE) | ~3KB + code |
838: 585: | Vue | .vue | Vite (IIFE) | ~35KB + code |
839: 586: | Svelte | .svelte | Vite (IIFE) | varies |
840: 587: 
841: 588: "Works forever" principle: framework code inlined into the plugin's .js file.
842: 589: The plugin never depends on what version of React/Vue/Preact the host app uses.
843: 590: 
844: 591: ---
845: 592: 
846: 593: ## Plugin Manifest Schema (Current — Flat Format)
847: 594: 
848: 595: ```json
849: 596: {
850: 597:   "name": "yt-feed",
851: 598:   "run": "bun plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/main.ts",
852: 599:   "hooks": ["feed.video"],
853: 600:   "methods": ["feed"],
854: 601:   "feeds": [
855: 602:     { "type": "video", "card": "yt-video-card" }
856: 603:   ]
857: 604: }
858: 605: ```
859: 606: 
860: 607: ### Fields
861: 608: | Field | Required | Description |
862: 609: |-------|----------|-------------|
863: 610: | `name` | ✅ | Unique plugin ID. Used in RPC routing, path derivation |
864: 611: | `version` | ❌ | Semver version. |
865: 612: | `description` | ❌ | Short description. |
866: 613: | `author` | ❌ | Creator name. |
867: 614: | `run` | ❌ | Command to spawn subprocess. Example: `"bun plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/main.ts"` |
868: 615: | `methods` | ❌ | Array of method prefixes for direct RPC routing. Example: `["feed", "login", "logout", "status"]` |
869: 616: | `hook` | ❌ | Alias for `hooks` (single string). Which hooks this plugin satisfies. |
870: 617: | `hooks` | ❌ | Array of hook strings. Which hooks this plugin satisfies. Example: `["feed.video", "auth"]` |
871: 618: | `ui` | ❌ | WC tag for main-UI rendering. Path: `build/plugins/<tag>.js`. App.tsx loads AND mounts this. |
872: 619: | `components` | ❌ | Array of WC tag names that need building but are neither `ui` nor `feeds[].card`. Example: `["yt-video-card"]` |
873: 620: | `feeds` | ❌ | Array of feed contribution objects. If present, this plugin is a feed source. |
874: 621: | `feeds[].type` | ✅ (if feeds) | Content type: `"video"`, `"image"`, `"post"`, etc. Also used as default hook for resolution. |
875: 622: | `feeds[].method` | ❌ | RPC method to call. Defaults to `methods[0]`. |
876: 623: | `feeds[].card` | ❌ | WC tag for rendering one item. Path: `build/plugins/<tag>.js`. If absent, items skipped. |
877: 624: 
878: 625: ### Plugin Types
879: 626: - **Backend-only**: Has `run` but no `ui`/`feeds` → spawned as subprocess, no UI
880: 627: - **Frontend-only (main UI)**: Has `ui` but no `run` → WC loaded and mounted by App.tsx
881: 628: - **Frontend-only (card/component)**: Has `components` or `feeds[].card` but no `run` → WC loaded by App.tsx, mounted by feed-widget
882: 629: - **Fullstack**: Has `run` + `ui`/`feeds` → subprocess + frontend components
883: 630: - **Feed source**: Has `run` + `feeds` → subprocess with feed method + card WC
884: 631: 
885: 632: **Frontend path derivation** (build time and runtime):
886: 633: - Build script collects tags from: `ui`, `components[]`, `feeds[*].card`
887: 634: - Output: `build/plugins/<tag>.js`
888: 635: - Search: plugin's own directory first, then cross-directory fallback by tag name
889: 636: 
890: 637: ### Example Manifests
891: 638: 
892: 639: **yt-feed (feed source, backend + card)**:

895: 642:   "name": "yt-feed",
896: 643:   "run": "bun plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/main.ts",
897: 644:   "hooks": ["feed.video"],
898: 645:   "methods": ["feed"],
899: 646:   "feeds": [{ "type": "video", "card": "yt-video-card" }]
900: 647: }
901: 648: ```

945: 692: ## Plugin Implementations
946: 693: 
947: 694: ### Phase 1/2 Demo Plugins (REMOVED FROM DISK — Historical Reference Only)
948: 695: - **greet-go** — Go backend (greet.hello, greet.bye). Frontend (greet-widget) removed in Phase 3. REMOVED from disk.
949: 696: - **logger-py** — Python backend (log.info, log.list). Frontend (log-viewer) removed in Phase 3. REMOVED from disk.
950: 697: - **joke-fetcher** — Bun/TS backend (joke.random, joke.types). REMOVED from disk.
951: 698: - **youtube-explorer** — Original monolithic YouTube plugin. Split into yt-feed, yt-auth, yt-search, yt-card. REMOVED from disk.
952: 699: 
953: 700: ### yt-feed — YouTube Feed Backend (Bun/TS)
954: 701: 
955: 702: #### Backend (plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/main.ts)
956: 703: - Uses Innertube API for YouTube home feed
957: 704: - Lazily loads cookie from shared file (`.youtube-cookie` written by yt-auth)
958: 705:   - Cookie read at request time, not startup — catches file written by yt-auth after process start
959: 706: - `feed` method: calls `tube.getHomeFeed()`, returns array of video items
960: 707: - Methods are simple (no prefix): just `"feed"` — prefix added by feed-widget as `name + "." + method`
961: 708: - 8s Promise.race timeout on API calls
962: 709: - No `feeds.method` in manifest — defaults to `methods[0]` ("feed")
963: 710: 
964: 711: ### yt-auth — YouTube Cookie Auth (Bun/TS)
965: 712: 
966: 713: #### Backend (plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-auth/main.ts)
967: 714: - Browser cookie database discovery:
968: 715:   - Firefox: finds `cookies.sqlite` via `find ~/.mozilla -name "cookies.sqlite" 2>/dev/null`
969: 716:   - Chrome/Chromium: tries sweet-cookie library, falls back to `find` for Cookies DB
970: 717: - Copies DB to temp file (avoids SQLite locking issues)
971: 718: - Queries: `SELECT name, value, host FROM moz_cookies WHERE host LIKE '%youtube.com'`
972: 719: - Extracts SAPISID cookie → constructs SAPISIDHASH Authorization header
973: 720: - Filters ST-* cookies (avoids 413 Request Entity Too Large on YouTube API)
974: 721: - Writes cookie to shared `.youtube-cookie` file (read by yt-feed)
975: 722: - Methods: `login` (discover+write), `logout` (delete file), `status` (check file exists)
976: 723: 
977: 724: ### yt-card — YouTube Video Card WC (React, no backend)
978: 725: 
979: 726: #### Frontend (plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-card/yt-video-card.tsx)
980: 727: - React card WC built via esbuild entry template
981: 728: - Receives item prop: `{ thumbnail, title, channel, viewCount, published }`
982: 729: - Renders thumbnail img, title H3, channel, views, published date
983: 730: - Handles click on thumbnail → calls `window.__pluginRpc("video-player.load", {url, title})` then dispatches `new CustomEvent("player-load", {detail: {url, title}})` on window
984: 731: - Player-modal listens for `player-load` to auto-open

2462: After tracing through the entire project, the root cause is clear:
2463: 
2464: ## Diagnosis
2465: 
2466: **The `uiPlugin` variable gets overwritten.** App.tsx iterates manifests and sets `uiPlugin = m` for *every* plugin that has a `ui` field. The last one wins:
2467: 
2468: ```
2469: feed       → ui: "feed-widget"   ← set first
2470: video-player → ui: "player-modal" ← overwrites
2471: yt-card    → ui: "yt-video-card"  ← overwrites again → FINAL uiPlugin
2472: ```
2473: 
2474: App.tsx creates an element for the **last** `uiPlugin` only — `<yt-video-card>`. The `<feed-widget>` element is **never created**. Feed shows "Loading..." because feed-widget's `loadFeed()` (called in connectedCallback) never runs.
2475: 
2476: `yt-video-card` receives `manifests` but expects `item` — renders nothing visible. The `#feed-container` has a single invisible card instead of the feed widget.
2477: 
2478: ## Three issues to fix
2479: 
2480: 1. **`yt-card/plugin.json` has `ui: "yt-video-card"`** — This is redundant. `yt-video-card` is already loaded via `yt-feed.feeds[0].card`. The `ui` field (wrongly) causes it to be mounted as a top-level view instead of staying a card component. Remove `ui` entirely.
2481: 
2482: 2. **`video-player/plugin.json` has `ui: "player-modal"`** — player-modal IS a legitimate overlay that needs DOM mounting (its `useEffect` listens for `player-load` events). Keep `ui` on this one.
2483: 
2484: 3. **App.tsx replaces `uiPlugin` instead of collecting them** — Change the loop to collect ALL manifests with `ui` into an array, then create+append elements for all of them in `#feed-container`.
2485: 
2486: ## Fix
2487: 
2488: ```diff
2489: - let uiPlugin: PluginManifest | null = null
2490: + const uiPlugins: PluginManifest[] = []
2491: ```
2492: 
2493: In the loop: `if (m.ui) { uiPlugins.push(m); /* load if not loaded */ }`
2494: 
2495: After the loop: create elements for ALL `uiPlugins`, not just one:
2496: 
2497: ```ts
2498: for (const m of uiPlugins) {
2499:   const tag = m.ui!
2500:   await customElements.whenDefined(tag)
2501:   const container = document.getElementById("feed-container")
2502:   if (container) {
2503:     const el = document.createElement(tag)
2504:     el.manifests = all
2505:     container.appendChild(el)
2506:   }
2507: }
2508: ```
2509: 
2510: Remove `ui: "yt-video-card"` from `yt-card/plugin.json`.
2511: 
2512: This makes:
2513: - `<feed-widget>` — renders the feed ✓
2514: - `<player-modal>` — renders nothing until `player-load` event ✓
2515: - `yt-video-card` — still loaded via feeds, used inside feed-widget items ✓

1045: 792: ## All Key Decisions Made (Chronological)
1046: 793: 
1047: 794: ### Architecture Decisions
1048: 795: 1. **Language-agnostic plugin system** — plugins can be written in any language (Go, Python, etc.)
1049: 796: 2. **Subprocess stdin/stdout JSON-RPC** — simplest cross-language IPC. Each plugin is a standalone process
1050: 797: 3. **No `jsonrpc` field** — messages are `{"id", "method", "params"}` only, cleaner than full JSON-RPC spec
1051: 798: 4. **Host routes by method prefix** — `"greet."` matches `"greet.hello"`. Plugin handles the specific action
1052: 799: 5. **Desktop first, mobile later** — subprocess works on desktop. Mobile will need FFI/Wasm
1053: 800: 6. **Different skeleton per platform is fine** — Electrobun for desktop, Tauri/zero-native for mobile. Plugins don't change
1054: 801: 7. **Everything is a plugin** — including frontend UI and eventually the skeleton itself
1055: 802: 8. **No "core" plugin** — just feature plugins (no separate plugin for core system functionality)
1056: 803: 9. **Companion app** (future) — a tiny binary that reads config and launches the right skeleton for the platform
1057: 804: 10. **Manifest scanning from plugins/*/plugin.json** — replaced config.json. Host reads all plugin.json files at startup via readdirSync + JSON.parse. No central config needed.
1058: 805: 11. **Flat manifest format** — no nested backend/frontend objects. All fields at top level. Matches VS Code/Chrome/Obsidian conventions.
1059: 806: 
1060: 807: ### Framework Decisions
1061: 808: 12. **Electrobun for prototyping** — easiest for a beginner (Bun/TypeScript). Native WebView, ~14MB bundle, fast startup
1062: 809: 13. **Tauri for future mobile** — Rust, mature ecosystem, iOS + Android support, but requires learning Rust
1063: 810: 14. **zero-native** (Vercel Labs) — alternative future option. Zig + system WebView, mobile support, but pre-release (v0.2)
1064: 811: 15. **WebUI (webui-dev)** — interesting but no mobile path. Opens a real browser (Chrome/Firefox), not a WebView. Few KB library
1065: 812: 16. **React + Tailwind + Vite** for the frontend (from the Electrobun template)
1066: 813: 
1067: 814: ### Phase 3 Decisions
1068: 815: 17. **Feed approach is THE approach** — old per-plugin widget cards are dead. App.tsx mounts only `<feed-widget>`. No WebComponentSlot, no plugin cards, no callMethod, no result box.
1069: 816: 18. **No library sharing needed** — one WC class definition is shared across all DOM instances. Framework bundle lives in prototype. Different plugins have different bundles (their own versions). No duplication within the same WC type. Option B (per-plugin shared library) solves a non-problem.
1070: 817: 19. **No `host.*` routing** — feed-widget does NOT call host RPCs. App.tsx calls host directly (`electroview.rpc.request.getPluginManifests({})`) and passes data via `.manifests` setter on the WC DOM element. `__pluginRpc` bridge stays simple: routes only to plugin subprocesses.
1071: 818: 20. **No fallback cards** — postponed. Only cards from plugins are rendered. Items from plugins without `card` field are skipped.
1072: 819: 21. **Data flow via property setters** — App.tsx uses `.manifests` setter, feed-widget uses `.item` setter on each card. Not via RPC, not via events.
1073: 820: 22. **`_item` naming convention** — private backing field with underscore prevents infinite loop in setter. `set item(data) { this._item = data; this._render() }`. Getter: `get item() { return this._item }`.
1074: 821: 23. **Simplified manifest** — `run` replaces `command`+`args`. `feeds` block replaces `frontendComponent`/`frontendFile`/`frontendSlot`. `ui` field for main-UI WC (only feed plugin uses it). No backward compat with old format.
1075: 822: 24. **Path derivation** — frontend file paths NOT in manifest. Derived at runtime: `plugins/<name>/frontend/<tag>.js`. Tag comes from `ui` or `feeds.card` field.
1076: 823: 25. **Feed is a plugin** — `plugins/feed/` with no backend. Users can swap feed implementation by installing a different feed plugin.
1077: 824: 26. **Framework agnostic cards** — each card WC is self-contained IIFE with framework inlined. React, Preact, Vue, Svelte all work.
1078: 825: 27. **No schema** — feed doesn't know or care about item structure. Raw data passes through to card WC. Cards written by the same person as the backend.
1079: 826: 28. **Auth in error banners** — feed-widget shows "Sign in" button in per-plugin error banners when plugin has `.auth.login` method. Calls it, reloads feed on success.
1080: 827: 29. **5 feed states** — loading, system error, empty, partial (some errors), loaded (all ok). Error banners per-plugin.
1081: 828: 
1082: 829: ### Plugin Design Decisions
1083: 830: 17. **Web Components for frontend plugins** — any framework (React, Vue, Svelte, Angular) can compile to them. Browser standard, no framework lock-in
1084: 831: 18. **Iframes as alternative** — stronger isolation, separate JS context, communication via postMessage. Heavier. Cannot display native UI (Qt/GTK)
1085: 832: 19. **Three plugin types** — `backend` (subprocess only), `frontend` (Web Component only), `fullstack` (both)
1086: 833: 20. **`window.__pluginRpc()` global bridge** — simplest way for any WC framework to call backend. No imports needed.
1087: 834: 21. **Centralized build script** — `scripts/build-plugins.js` handles all plugin types. One command for all.
1088: 835: 22. **`findProjectRoot()` walks up from `import.meta.dir`** — works in both dev (flat) and bundled modes
1089: 836: 23. **FileSink.write() for plugin stdin** — Bun's `Subprocess.stdin` is a `FileSink` when piped. Use `.write()` directly.
1090: 837: 24. **RPC params typed as `unknown`** — Electrobun's `defineRPC` expects `(params?: unknown) => unknown`. All handlers cast internally.
1091: 838: 
1092: 839: ### Go Plugin Specific
1093: 840: 25. **`*json.RawMessage` for params** — user explicitly chose this over simpler `map[string]interface{}`. More type safety, more verbose.
1094: 841: 26. **Nested struct for params** — each method defines its own params struct, unmarshals from RawMessage
1095: 842: 
1096: 843: ### Teaching/Communication Decisions
1097: 844: 27. **User is a beginner** — assume ZERO prior knowledge. Explain every concept, syntax, and line
1098: 845: 28. **Provide full code in messages** — user copies code themselves. Never modify files without explicit permission
1099: 846: 29. **Line-by-line explanation tables** — after every code block, explain each section in a table
1100: 847: 30. **Multi-level zoom** — big picture → file → scope/block → line → symbol → syntax construct
1101: 848: 31. **Be proactive** — research tools, patterns, pitfalls without being asked. Suggest better approaches
1102: 849: 32. **Mentor, not yes-man** — correct wrong assumptions directly. Lead the project in the right direction
1103: 850: 33. **Test standalone before integrating** — catch plugin bugs in isolation before running the full app
1104: 851: 34. **No code comments unless asked** — don't add comments to code files
1105: 852: 35. **Plan mode = read-only, Build mode = can write** — plan mode explains and provides code in messages, build mode can create/edit files + run commands
1106: 853: 36. **Never commit unless asked** — no git operations without explicit instruction
1107: 854: 37. **Two-file rule** — only modify AGENTS.md (project knowledge) and SKILL.md (general rules). Never touch project code.
1108: 855: 38. **Update both files every prompt** — actively check for changes. Never assume "last agent handled it."
1109: 856: 
1110: 857: ### Session 2026-07-07 Decisions (Plugin Refactor — youtube-explorer split, hooks, components, feeds array)
1111: 858: 39. **`components` manifest field** — separates build concern from mount concern. `ui` → build AND mount (views). `components` → build only (cards, sub-components). Fixes the Single-Field Conflation Antipattern where `ui` was the only way to trigger a build.
1112: 859: 40. **`hooks` manifest field** — decentralized capability discovery. A plugin declares what hooks it satisfies (e.g., `"feed.video"`, `"auth"`, `"search"`, `"player"`). The host resolves hooks at runtime. Replaces hardcoded method prefix routing for capability discovery.
1113: 860: 41. **`callHook`/`resolveHook` RPC handlers** — new host RPCs for hook-based discovery. `callHook` finds the first plugin matching a hook and calls its method. Enables feed-widget to use `callHook("feed.video")` instead of iterating manifests.

1133: 1: # React + Tailwind + Vite Electrobun Template
1134: 2: 
1135: 3: A fast Electrobun desktop app template with React, Tailwind CSS, and Vite for hot module replacement (HMR).
1136: 4: 
1137: 5: ## Getting Started
1138: 6: 
1139: 7: ```bash
1140: 8: # Install dependencies
1141: 9: bun install
1142: 10: 
1143: 11: # Development without HMR (uses bundled assets)
1144: 12: bun run dev
1145: 13: 
1146: 14: # Development with HMR (recommended)
1147: 15: bun run dev:hmr
1148: 16: 
1149: 17: # Build for production
1150: 18: bun run build
1151: 19: 
1152: 20: # Build for production release
1153: 21: bun run build:prod
1154: 22: ```
1155: 23: 
1156: 24: ## How HMR Works
1157: 25: 
1158: 26: When you run `bun run dev:hmr`:
1159: 27: 
1160: 28: 1. **Vite dev server** starts on `http://localhost:5173` with HMR enabled
1161: 29: 2. **Electrobun** starts and detects the running Vite server
1162: 30: 3. The app loads from the Vite dev server instead of bundled assets
1163: 31: 4. Changes to React components update instantly without full page reload
1164: 32: 
1165: 33: When you run `bun run dev` (without HMR):
1166: 34: 
1167: 35: 1. Electrobun starts and loads from `views://mainview/index.html`
1168: 36: 2. You need to rebuild (`bun run build`) to see changes
1169: 37: 
1170: 38: ## Project Structure
1171: 39: 
1172: 40: ```
1173: 41: ├── src/
1174: 42: │   ├── bun/
1175: 43: │   │   └── index.ts        # Main process (Electrobun/Bun)
1176: 44: │   └── mainview/
1177: 45: │       ├── App.tsx         # React app component
1178: 46: │       ├── main.tsx        # React entry point

1342: 861: 42. **`feeds` as array** — `feeds: [{type:"video", card:"yt-video-card"}]` (was a single object). Enables a single plugin to contribute to multiple feed types. The `feeds-as-array` future plan is now implemented.
1343: 862: 43. **Plugin nesting** — plugins can live under other plugins: `plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/`. The host uses recursive directory scanning (`getAllPluginManifests`). Parent `plugin.json` (youtube) has metadata only. Enables logical grouping.
1344: 863: 44. **Monolithic plugin split** — `youtube-explorer` (one big plugin) split into `yt-feed`, `yt-auth`, `yt-search`, `yt-card`. Each has a single responsibility. yt-feed handles feed, yt-auth handles auth, yt-search handles search, yt-card provides the video card WC.
1345: 864: 45. **Lazy cookie reload** — yt-feed re-reads cookie file on each request if `cookieStr` is null. Catches file written by yt-auth after startup. Fixes the "auth before feed" timing issue for long-lived processes.
1346: 865: 46. **`name + "." + method` RPC prefix** — feed-widget calls `__pluginRpc("yt-feed.feed")` instead of `__pluginRpc("feed")`. The host splits on first dot to find plugin by `config.name`. This is needed because simple method names ("feed", "list") would overlap between plugins.
1347: 866: 47. **Sign-in button searches ALL manifests** — feed-widget searches `manifests.find(m => m.methods?.includes("login"))` rather than checking only the errored source's methods. Auth methods live on a separate plugin (yt-auth) from the feed source (yt-feed).
1348: 867: 48. **`components` as declarative ownership** — when source not found in referencing dir, use `components` field on the owning plugin's manifest. yt-card declares `components: ["yt-video-card"]` so the build script finds the source in yt-card's directory.
1349: 868: 49. **Build output path changed** — frontend JS loads from `build/plugins/<tag>.js` (was `plugins/<name>/frontend/<tag>.js`). Centralized build output directory. Host security restricts `getPluginFrontend` to `build/plugins/` path.
1350: 869: 50. **Vite as universal build tool** — replaced ad-hoc esbuild-only approach. Now all frameworks (React, Preact, Vue, Svelte) build via Vite IIFE. Build script auto-detects framework by scanning imports in source files.
1351: 870: 51. **Build script entry template includes `_manifests`** — all WCs get both `_item` and `_manifests` setters. Allows any WC to access the full manifests array for self-discovery.
1352: 871: 52. **Player modal uses `<iframe>`** — embed URLs from YouTube/PeerTube are HTML pages, not direct media files. `<video>` tag cannot play them. iframe is the standard approach for embed URLs.
1353: 872: 53. **Event bridge for card→modal** — cards dispatch `CustomEvent("player-load", {detail: {url, title}})` on `window`. Player-modal listens in `useEffect(() => { window.addEventListener("player-load", handler) })`. Decoupled communication.
1354: 873: 54. **Plugin UI elements created imperatively** — App.tsx uses `document.getElementById("feed-container")` and `document.createElement(tag)` instead of React refs or JSX. WCs created outside React's VDOM to avoid framework conflicts.
1355: 874: 55. **No `frontend/` subdirectory** — source files alongside `plugin.json` (e.g., `plugins/feed/feed-widget.tsx`). The build script finds source by `<dir>/<tag>.<ext>`. Previously required `frontend/` subdirectory.
1356: 875: 56. **Recursive manifest scanning** — `getAllPluginManifests()` walks directory tree recursively. Supports nested plugins under `plugins/*/plugins/*/`. Flat scan (`readdirSync(plugins/*)`) doesn't find deeply nested manifests.

1360: 879: ## Bug History
1361: 880: 
1362: 881: ### Bug #1: `for...in` instead of `for...of` (stdout reader)
1363: 882: - **Location**: `readStdout()` and `readStderr()` in index.ts
1364: 883: - **Problem**: `for (const line in lines)` iterates over array INDICES as strings ("0", "1"), not actual line values
1365: 884: - **Fix**: Change to `for (const line of lines)`
1366: 885: - **Impact**: Plugin responses silently dropped. `JSON.parse("0")` returns `0`, then `0.id != null` is false, so every request times out after 10 seconds
1367: 886: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED
1368: 887: 
1369: 888: ### Bug #2: `==` instead of `=` (alive flag)
1370: 889: - **Location**: `proc.exited.then()` callback
1371: 890: - **Problem**: `plugin.alive == false` is a comparison, not an assignment. The expression evaluates to `true` or `false` but the value is discarded. `alive` is never set to false
1372: 891: - **Fix**: Change `==` to `=`
1373: 892: - **Impact**: When a plugin crashes, the health check never detects it. Plugin stays marked as alive forever
1374: 893: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED
1375: 894: 
1376: 895: ### Bug #3: Extra `}` in template literal
1377: 896: - **Location**: Console error message in exit handler
1378: 897: - **Problem**: `` `[${pc.name}] exited (code ${code}})` `` — extra `}` after `${code}`
1379: 898: - **Fix**: Remove the extra `}`
1380: 899: - **Impact**: Output shows `"exited (code 0})"` instead of `"exited (code 0)"`
1381: 900: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED
1382: 901: 
1383: 902: ### Bug #4: Missing `pendingRequests.delete()`
1384: 903: - **Location**: `handlePluginResponse()` in index.ts
1385: 904: - **Problem**: After resolving/rejecting a pending request, the entry stays in the Map forever
1386: 905: - **Fix**: Add `pendingRequests.delete(msg.id)` after `clearTimeout(pending.timer)`
1387: 906: - **Impact**: Memory leak. Over time, the Map fills with resolved requests
1388: 907: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED
1389: 908: 
1390: 909: ### Bug #5 (Frontend): `pluginList` instead of `pluginRequest`
1391: 910: - **Location**: App.tsx, `callMethod()` function
1392: 911: - **Problem**: `electroview.rpc?.request.pluginList({ method, params })` calls the wrong RPC method
1393: 912: - **Fix**: Change to `electroview.rpc.request.pluginRequest({ method, params })` and remove unnecessary `?.`
1394: 913: - **Impact**: Clicking a method button shows the plugin list instead of calling the plugin
1395: 914: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED
1396: 915: 
1397: 916: ### Bug #6 (Python): Inconsistent indentation
1398: 917: - **Location**: `logger-py/main.py`, lines 11 and 13
1399: 918: - **Problem**: 6 spaces of indentation instead of 8 (Python requires consistent indentation level for if/else bodies)
1400: 919: - **Fix**: Change from 6 spaces to 8 spaces (4 for function body + 4 for if/else body)
1401: 920: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED
1402: 921: 
1403: 922: ### Bug #7 (Python): Missing default for `params.get()`
1404: 923: - **Location**: `logger-py/main.py`, line 20
1405: 924: - **Problem**: `params = request.get("params")` — if the request has no "params" key, `params` becomes `None`. Then `params.get("message", "")` crashes with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get'`
1406: 925: - **Fix**: `params = request.get("params", {})` — default to empty dict

1409: 928: ### Bug #8: Vite outDir doubled path
1410: 929: - **Location**: Generated `.vite.config.mjs` in `build-plugins.js`
1411: 930: - **Problem**: Setting `root` to plugin dir AND `build.outDir` relative to root caused path like `plugins/logger-py/frontend/plugins/logger-py/frontend/`
1412: 931: - **Fix**: Set `build.outDir` to `"."` (current directory = root) and `emptyOutDir: false`
1413: 932: - **Impact**: Vite build failed for Vue plugins — couldn't find output directory
1414: 933: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED

1416: 935: ### Bug #9: Electrobun build.copy "plugins/**" doesn't work in dev mode
1417: 936: - **Location**: `electrobun.config.ts` copy rules
1418: 937: - **Problem**: The glob `"plugins/**"` in `build.copy` only works during production build. In dev mode, the copy step is skipped.
1419: 938: - **Fix**: Harmless — `resolvePath()` resolves files from source tree directly in dev mode
1420: 939: - **Impact**: None (works correctly, just different resolution paths per mode)
1421: 940: - **Status**: ✅ NO FIX NEEDED
1422: 941: 
1423: 942: ### Bug #10: Subprocess.stdin is a FileSink, not WritableStream
1424: 943: - **Location**: `sendToPlugin()` in index.ts
1425: 944: - **Problem**: Bun's `Subprocess.stdin` when piped returns a `FileSink`, not a `WritableStream`. Calling `.getWriter()` on it fails: "FileSink doesn't have getWriter"
1426: 945: - **Fix**: Check `typeof stdin !== "number"`, then call `stdin.write(msg)` directly. No `getWriter()`/`releaseLock()`.
1427: 946: - **Impact**: Plugin requests silently failed to send. Plugin never received request, so every request timed out.
1428: 947: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED
1429: 948: 
1430: 949: ### Bug #11: RPC handler params type must be `unknown`
1431: 950: - **Location**: All 4 RPC handler definitions in index.ts
1432: 951: - **Problem**: Electrobun's `defineRPC()` strictly expects `(params?: unknown) => unknown`. Using specific types causes TypeScript errors.
1433: 952: - **Fix**: Declare all handlers as `async (params: unknown) => { ... }` and cast internally with `params as { method: string; params: any }`
1434: 953: - **Impact**: TypeScript compilation errors. App wouldn't build.
1435: 954: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED
1436: 955: 
1437: 956: ### Bug #12 (CRITICAL): Frontend RPC timeout default too short for slow plugins
1438: 957: - **Location**: `src/mainview/App.tsx`, line 7 — `Electroview.defineRPC({})`
1439: 958: - **Problem**: `Electroview.defineRPC()` with no `maxRequestTime` defaults to a very short timeout (~1s). The youtube-explorer feed request takes ~2.5s (Innertube.create 1.3s + getHomeFeed 1.2s). The frontend's RPC timer fired before the plugin response arrived. The host received the response and resolved it (visible in terminal logs `handleResponse pending=true`), but the frontend had already thrown "RPC request timed out." — the response was discarded because nobody was listening.
1440: 959: - **Fix**: Added `maxRequestTime: 20000` to BOTH `BrowserView.defineRPC()` (host, was already 15000) AND `Electroview.defineRPC()` (frontend, was missing). The frontend timeout must be >= all inner timeouts combined.
1441: 960: - **Impact**: Every `youtube.feed` request silently failed. User saw "Loading feed..." for ~1s then "RPC request timed out." even though the plugin processed the request successfully. Only visible in WebView dev console (F12) — no terminal log.
1442: 961: - **Lesson**: Every RPC layer must have a timeout >= all the layers below it combined. Always set explicit `maxRequestTime` on EVERY `defineRPC()` call.
1443: 962: - **Related fixes applied**: readStdout buffer fix (already done), readStderr buffer fix (was still broken — same `lines.pop()` pattern), event queue with knownIds dedup (defeats Bun canary stdin re-delivery bug), feedLoadedRef guard (React double-mount protection)
1444: 963: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED
1445: 964: 
1446: 965: ### Bug #13: Single `uiPlugin` variable overwritten by last manifest with `ui`
1447: 966: - **Location**: `App.tsx` — `let uiPlugin: PluginManifest | null = null`
1448: 967: - **Problem**: Loop iterated manifests and set `uiPlugin = m` for each plugin with `ui` field. Last one won (yt-card's `yt-video-card` overrides feed's `feed-widget`). feed-widget element never created.
1449: 968: - **Fix**: Changed to `uiPlugins[]` array, loop over all, create elements for ALL UI plugins, not just the last one.
1450: 969: - **Impact**: White screen — feed-widget never mounted. Only `<yt-video-card>` created (renders nothing without item).
1451: 970: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED
1452: 971: 
1453: 972: ### Bug #14: `yt-card/plugin.json` uses `ui` field for card component
1454: 973: - **Location**: `plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-card/plugin.json` — `ui: "yt-video-card"`
1455: 974: - **Problem**: `ui` field caused both loading AND mounting. yt-video-card is a card component, not a standalone view. But removing `ui` broke the build (build script couldn't find source).
1456: 975: - **Fix**: Removed `ui`, added `components: ["yt-video-card"]` to manifest. Build script collects from `components` too.
1457: 976: - **Impact**: Stale build — yt-video-card.js never rebuilt after dispatchEvent added, because build script couldn't find a tag referencing yt-video-card.
1458: 977: - **Design decision**: New `components` field separates "build this WC" from "mount this WC"
1459: 978: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED

1461: 980: ### Bug #15: Sign-in button not appearing for yt-feed auth errors
1462: 981: - **Location**: `feed-widget.tsx` — `source?.methods?.includes("login")`
1463: 982: - **Problem**: Error came from `yt-feed` (methods: `["feed"]`), but login method is on `yt-auth` (different plugin). Source methods don't include "login". Sign-in button never showed.
1464: 983: - **Fix**: Search ALL manifests for a plugin with `"login"` in methods: `manifests.find(m => m.methods?.includes("login"))`.
1465: 984: - **Impact**: User sees "Not authenticated" but no way to sign in.
1466: 985: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED

1468: 987: ### Bug #16: yt-feed doesn't re-read cookie after login
1469: 988: - **Location**: `plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-feed/main.ts`
1470: 989: - **Problem**: yt-feed read cookie only at process startup (`const cached = loadCookie()`). After yt-auth wrote cookie to shared file, yt-feed's `cookieStr` was still null.
1471: 990: - **Fix**: Lazy reload in "feed" handler: `if (!cookieStr) { const fresh = loadCookie(); if (fresh) cookieStr = fresh }`.
1472: 991: - **Impact**: Even after successful login, feed says "Not authenticated" because yt-feed never re-reads the cookie file.
1473: 992: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED

1475: 994: ### Bug #17: yt-video-card never dispatches `player-load` event
1476: 995: - **Location**: `plugins/youtube/plugins/yt-card/yt-video-card.tsx` — `handleClick()`
1477: 996: - **Problem**: `handleClick` called RPC but had no `dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("player-load", ...))`. Player-modal was never notified.
1478: 997: - **Fix**: Added `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("player-load", { detail: { url, title } }))` after RPC call.
1479: 998: - **Impact**: Clicking yt-video-card did nothing. peertube-card already had dispatchEvent and worked.

1482: 1001: ### Bug #18: Player-modal uses `<video>` with embed URLs
1483: 1002: - **Location**: `plugins/video-player/player-modal.tsx`
1484: 1003: - **Problem**: Both services passed embed page URLs (`youtube.com/embed/...`, `peertube.cpy.re/videos/embed/...`). `<video>` expects direct media file URLs.
1485: 1004: - **Fix**: Changed `<video src={...}>` to `<iframe src={...}>`.
1486: 1005: - **Impact**: Player-modal showed but video didn't play (blank/error).
1487: 1006: - **Status**: ✅ FIXED
1488: 1007: 
1489: 1008: ### Bug #19: Build script can't find source across directories (stale build)
1490: 1009: - **Location**: `scripts/build-plugins.ts`
1491: 1010: - **Problem**: When `yt-feed`'s manifest referenced `card: "yt-video-card"`, build script searched for source only in yt-feed's directory → not found → skip. Source was in yt-card's directory. yt-card no longer had `ui` → no tags → nothing built. Stale `.js` persisted.
1492: 1011: - **Fix**: yt-card declares `components: ["yt-video-card"]` → build script finds tag from `components[]` → finds source in yt-card's dir. Cross-directory ownership via `components` field.

1508: 1027: ### Development Tools Suggested
1509: 1028: | Tool | Purpose | Why |
1510: 1029: |------|---------|-----|
1511: 1030: | **jq** | CLI JSON processor | Parse and format plugin JSON output during testing |
1512: 1031: | **watchexec** | File watcher | Auto-restart app when plugin source files change |
1513: 1032: | **hyperfine** | Benchmarking | Measure plugin response times |
1514: 1033: | **just / make** | Task runner | Replace long shell commands with named tasks |
1515: 1034: | **uv** | Python package manager | Faster than pip, useful for Python plugins |
1516: 1035: | **asdf / mise** | Version manager | Manage Go, Python, Rust versions per project |
1517: 1036: | **printf** | Shell command | Send JSON-RPC messages to plugin stdin for standalone testing |
1518: 1037: 
1519: 1038: ### Frontend Plugin Approaches
1520: 1039: | Approach | Isolation | Performance | Framework Lock-in | Communication |
1521: 1040: |----------|-----------|-------------|-------------------|---------------|
1522: 1041: | **Web Components** | Medium | Lightweight | None (standard) | Direct function calls |
1523: 1042: | **iframe** | High (separate JS context) | Heavier | None | postMessage async |
1524: 1043: | **Dynamic React import** | Low (same context) | Lightweight | React only | Direct imports |
1525: 1044: 
1526: 1045: ### iframe Details
1527: 1046: - Embeds a completely separate HTML document within the current page
1528: 1047: - Has its OWN JavaScript engine, its own DOM, its own CSS
1529: 1048: - CANNOT access or modify the host page's DOM (unless same-origin)
1530: 1049: - Communication only via `window.parent.postMessage()` and `window.addEventListener("message", ...)`
1531: 1050: - Can be sandboxed with `sandbox` attribute (restrict scripts, forms, popups, etc.)
1532: 1051: - Cannot display native UI (Qt, GTK, WinForms). Only HTML/CSS/JS
1533: 1052: - Each iframe consumes memory for a separate JS engine instance
1534: 1053:

1539: 1058: - "You Don't Know JS" series — JavaScript depth

1658: 1177: ## Teaching/Communication Rules (for agents working here)
1659: 1178: 
1660: 1179: ### The Two-File Rule (ABSOLUTE)
1661: 1180: 1. **MODIFY ONLY** `AGENTS.md` (project-specific knowledge) and `~/.config/opencode/skills/coding/SKILL.md` (general coding rules)
1662: 1181: 2. **NEVER TOUCH** any other project file — the user handles ALL code
1663: 1182: 3. **UPDATE BOTH FILES EVERY PROMPT** — actively check if anything changed. See the "Auto-Update Protocol" in SKILL.md.
1664: 1183: 4. **Always verify** — never assume "the last agent already updated this"
1665: 1184: 
1666: 1185: ### Teaching Style
1667: 1186: 1. **User is a beginner** — assume ZERO prior knowledge. Explain every concept, every syntax construct, every line
1668: 1187: 2. **Provide full code in messages** — user copies code themselves. Never modify files without explicit build mode permission
1669: 1188: 3. **Line-by-line explanation tables** — after every code block, explain each section in a table
1670: 1189: 4. **Multi-level zoom** — big picture → file → block → line → symbol → syntax construct
1671: 1190: 5. **Re-read files before every response** — stay in sync with what the user has written
1672: 1191: 6. **Research before speaking** — check latest docs for libraries, APIs, frameworks. Don't guess
1673: 1192: 7. **Surface better approaches** — if there's a better way, explain the tradeoffs and let the user decide
1674: 1193: 8. **Be proactive** — research and suggest relevant tools, patterns, and pitfalls without being asked
1675: 1194: 9. **Mentor, don't just answer** — correct wrong assumptions directly. Lead the project
1676: 1195: 10. **Test standalone before integrating** — always suggest testing plugins in isolation first
1677: 1196: 11. **No code comments unless asked** — don't add comments to source files
1678: 1197: 12. **Never commit unless asked** — no git operations without explicit instruction
1679: 1198: 13. **Never force push to main/master** — warn user if they request this
1680: 1199: 14. **Never amend unless the commit was just created by you and not pushed** — make a new commit for hook rejections

1702: 1221: ### Plugin Types
1703: 1222: - `backend` — only a subprocess, no UI contribution
1704: 1223: - `frontend` — only a Web Component, no subprocess
1705: 1224: - `fullstack` — both backend subprocess AND frontend Web Component
1706: 1225: 
1707: 1226: ### Slots (for frontend components)
1708: 1227: - `main` — primary content area (where plugin widgets display)
1709: 1228: - Future: `sidebar`, `header`, `statusbar`, `settings`

1711: 1230: ---
1712: 1231: 
1713: 1232: ## Phase 3 Architecture: Unified Feed
1714: 1233: 
1715: 1234: ### Core Shift
1716: 1235: Phase 1-2 built per-plugin standalone widgets (each plugin in its own card, rendered by App.tsx).
1717: 1236: Phase 3 replaces this with a SINGLE feed that aggregates items from all content plugins.
1718: 1237: 
1719: 1238: The feed itself is a plugin (`plugins/feed/`), swappable by the user. It has no backend — just a
1720: 1239: frontend Web Component (`feed-widget`). App.tsx loads manifests from the host, loads all frontend
1721: 1240: JS from `build/plugins/`, creates UI WC elements imperatively in a container div (passing manifests
1722: 1241: via `.manifests` setter). Feed-widget discovers feed-contributing plugins, calls their feed methods
1723: 1242: via `callHook()` or `__pluginRpc("name.method")`, and renders their card WCs.
1724: 1243: 
1725: 1244: Each content plugin provides:
1726: 1245: - **Backend**: RPC method that returns feed items (any shape)
1727: 1246: - **Frontend**: A Web Component "card" that renders ONE feed item
1728: 1247: - **Manifest**: Declares `feeds` array, `hooks` for capability discovery, `components` for WC tags
1729: 1248: 
1730: 1249: ### Architecture Diagram
1731: 1250: ```
1732: 1251: ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
1733: 1252: │  WebView (React + Tailwind + Vite HMR)                          │
1734: 1253: │                                                                  │
1735: 1254: │  App.tsx:                                                        │
1736: 1255: │  1. electroview.rpc.request.getPluginManifests({}) → manifests   │
1737: 1256: │  2. Collects WC tags: feeds[].card + ui → dedup                  │
1738: 1257: │  3. For each tag: loadFrontend("build/plugins/<tag>.js")         │
1739: 1258: │     (getPluginFrontend → <script> → customElements.define())     │
1740: 1259: │  4. Builds uiPlugins[] = manifests with ui field                 │
1741: 1260: │  5. For each ui plugin: createElement(tag), set .manifests,      │
1742: 1261: │     appendChild to #feed-container (imperative, not React)       │
1743: 1262: │         │                                                        │
1744: 1263: │         ▼                                                        │
1745: 1264: │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
1746: 1265: │  │ <feed-widget> (plugin: feed/)                        │        │
1747: 1266: │  │ set manifests(data) {                                │        │
1748: 1267: │  │   this._manifests = data;                            │        │
1749: 1268: │  │   this.loadFeed(); // trigger re-fetch               │        │
1750: 1269: │  │ }                                                    │        │
1751: 1270: │  │                                                      │        │
1752: 1271: │  │ loadFeed():                                          │        │
1753: 1272: │  │   1. Filter _manifests by has feeds[]                 │        │
1754: 1273: │  │   2. For each source:                                │        │
1755: 1274: │  │      a. __pluginRpc(name + "." + method, {})         │        │
1756: 1275: │  │      b. Receives items (any shape, no schema)         │        │
1757: 1276: │  │   3. Merges items (by source order)                   │        │
1758: 1277: │  │   4. For each item:                                   │        │
1759: 1278: │  │      cr = document.createElement(feeds[0].card)      │        │
1760: 1279: │  │      cr.item = rawItem (ALL data)                     │        │
1761: 1280: │  │      feedContainer.appendChild(cr)                   │        │
1762: 1281: │  │                                                      │        │
1763: 1282: │  │ States: loading|error|empty|partial|loaded           │        │
1764: 1283: │  │ Error banners with Sign In (searches all manifests   │        │
1765: 1284: │  │ for plugin with "login" method, not just source)     │        │
1766: 1285: │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
1767: 1286: │                                                                  │
1768: 1287: │  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────┐  ┌──────────────┐   │
1769: 1288: │  │ yt-video-card    │  │ peertube-card    │  │ player-modal │   │
1770: 1289: │  │ (from yt-card)   │  │ (from peertube)  │  │ (from vid-   │   │
1771: 1290: │  │ React 18         │  │ React 18         │  │  player)     │   │
1772: 1291: │  │ click→player-load│  │ click→player-load│  │ Listens for  │   │
1773: 1292: │  │ custom event     │  │ custom event     │  │ player-load  │   │
1774: 1293: │  └──────────────────┘  └──────────────────┘  └──────────────┘   │
1775: 1294: │                                                                  │
1776: 1295: │  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐        │
1777: 1296: │  │ player-modal (ui: "player-modal", created in #feed- │        │
1778: 1297: │  │ container by App.tsx alongside feed-widget)         │        │
1779: 1298: │  │ - Listens for "player-load" event on window        │        │
1780: 1299: │  │ - Opens iframe modal when event fires               │        │
1781: 1300: │  │ - Closes on Escape / click-outside / close button   │        │
1782: 1301: │  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘        │
1783: 1302: └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
1784: 1303: ```
1785: 1304: 
1786: 1305: ### Data Flow (Detailed)
1787: 1306: 1. **App.tsx mounts** → `electroview.rpc.request.getPluginManifests({})` → gets array of all manifests
1788: 1307: 2. **App.tsx collects WC tags**: for each manifest, collects `feeds[*].card` and `ui` tags (dedup)
1789: 1308: 3. **App.tsx loads frontend JS**: for each unique tag:
1790: 1309:    - Calls `electroview.rpc.request.getPluginFrontend({ path: "build/plugins/<tag>.js" })`
1791: 1310:    - Creates `<script>` element, sets `textContent` = JS code, appends to `<body>`
1792: 1311:    - `customElements.define()` registers the WC globally
1793: 1312: 4. **App.tsx creates UI elements**: builds `uiPlugins[]` (manifests with `ui`), waits for each WC definition, creates element via `document.createElement(tag)`, sets `el.manifests = all`, appends to `#feed-container` div
1794: 1313: 5. **feed-widget receives manifests**: via `.manifests` setter (set by App.tsx's imperative code) → triggers `loadFeed()`

58: fn discover_plugins(dir: &PathBuf) -> Vec<(PluginManifest, PathBuf)> {
59:     let mut results = Vec::new();
60:     if !dir.exists() {
61:         return results;
62:     }
63:     for entry in std::fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap() {
64:         let entry = entry.unwrap();
65:         let path = entry.path();
66:         if path.is_dir() {
67:             let plugin_json = path.join("plugin.json");
68:             if plugin_json.exists() {
69:                 if let Ok(content) = std::fs::read_to_string(&plugin_json) {
70:                     if let Ok(manifest) =
71:                         serde_json::from_str::<PluginManifest>(&content)
72:                     {
73:                         results.push((manifest, path.clone()));
74:                     }
75:                 }
76:             }
77:             results.extend(discover_plugins(&path));
78:         }
79:     }
80:     results
81: }

85: fn resolve_run(run: &str, plugin_dir: &PathBuf) -> (String, Vec<String>) {
86:     let parts: Vec<&str> = run.split_whitespace().collect();
87:     let cmd = parts[0].to_string();

93:             } else {
94:                 a.to_string()
95:             }
96:         })
97:         .collect();
98:     (cmd, args)
99: }

170:     params: Option<Value>,
171: ) -> Result<Value, String> {
172:     let dot = method
173:         .find('.')
174:         .ok_or_else(|| "Method must be in 'name.action' format".to_string())?;
175:     let plugin_name = &method[..dot];
176:     let action = &method[dot + 1..];
177: 
178:     let mut plugins = state.plugins.lock().await;
179:     let plugin = plugins
180:         .iter_mut()
181:         .find(|p| p.name == plugin_name)
182:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("Plugin not found: {}", plugin_name))?;
183: 
184:     let id = plugin.next_id.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst);
185:     let (tx, rx) = oneshot::channel();
186:     plugin.pending.lock().await.insert(id, tx);
187: 
188:     let msg = serde_json::json!({
189:         "id": id,
190:         "method": action,
191:         "params": params.unwrap_or(serde_json::json!({})),
192:     });
193:     let mut line = serde_json::to_string(&msg).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
194:     line.push('\n');
195:     plugin
196:         .stdin
197:         .lock()
198:         .await
199:         .write_all(line.as_bytes())
200:         .await
201:         .map_err(|e| format!("stdin write error: {}", e))?;
202: 
203:     drop(plugins); // release lock so reader task can access pending
204: 
205:     timeout(Duration::from_secs(15), rx)
206:         .await
207:         .map_err(|_| "Plugin request timed out".to_string())?
208:         .map_err(|_| "Plugin request cancelled".to_string())?
209: }
210: 
211: // -- Tauri command: resolve_hook --
212: //   invoke("resolve_hook", { hook: "feed.video" })
213: 
214: #[tauri::command]
215: async fn resolve_hook(
216:     state: tauri::State<'_, AppState>,
217:     hook: String,
218: ) -> Result<Value, String> {
219:     let plugins = state.plugins.lock().await;
220:     let plugin = plugins
221:         .iter()
222:         .find(|p| p.hooks.contains(&hook))
223:         .ok_or_else(|| format!("No plugin provides hook: {}", hook))?;
224: 
225:     Ok(serde_json::json!({
226:         "name": plugin.name,
227:         "methods": plugin.methods,
228:     }))
229: }
230: 
231: // -- Tauri command: call_hook --
232: //   invoke("call_hook", { hook: "feed.video", method: "feed", params: {} })
233: //   method and params are both optional
234: 
235: #[tauri::command]
236: async fn call_hook(
237:     state: tauri::State<'_, AppState>,
238:     hook: String,
239:     method: Option<String>,
240:     params: Option<Value>,
241: ) -> Result<Value, String> {
242:     let (plugin_name, plugin_methods) = {
243:         let plugins = state.plugins.lock().await;
244:         let plugin = plugins
245:             .iter()
246:             .find(|p| p.hooks.contains(&hook))
247:             .ok_or_else(|| format!("No plugin provides hook: {}", hook))?;
248:         (plugin.name.clone(), plugin.methods.clone())
249:     };
250: 
251:     let action = method.unwrap_or(
252:         plugin_methods
253:             .first()
254:             .ok_or_else(|| format!("Plugin '{}' has no methods", plugin_name))?
255:             .clone(),
256:     );
257:     let full_method = format!("{}.{}", plugin_name, action);
258: 
259:     plugin_request(state, full_method, params).await
260: }
261:

267:         .parent()

273: 
274:     tauri::Builder::default()

276:         .setup(move |app| {
277:             let handles = tauri::async_runtime::block_on(async {
278:                 let mut handles = Vec::new();
279:                 for (manifest, plugin_dir) in &discovered {
280:                     if manifest.run.is_some() {

282:                         {

285:                                 handles.push(handle);
286:                             }

292:                             }

298: 
299:             println!(

301:                 handles.len()
302:             );
303:             app.manage(AppState {

306:             Ok(())

4225: yt-feed runs as a long-lived process. It reads the cookie at startup:
4226: ```tsx
4227: const cached = loadCookie()
4228: if (cached) {
4229:   // create tube, try to get account info

4235: ```tsx

4239: ```
4240: 
4241: If `cookieStr` is null (no cookie at startup), it returns "Not authenticated". Even after yt-auth writes the cookie file, yt-feed's `cookieStr` is still null because it's an in-memory variable — the process doesn't reload on file change.
4242: 
4243: **This is the root cause!** yt-feed caches the cookie at startup and never re-reads the file. After yt-auth writes the cookie, yt-feed still has `cookieStr = null`.
4244: 
4245: The fix: yt-feed should re-read the cookie file on each "feed" request, not just at startup. Or yt-auth's "login" should signal yt-feed to reload.

4247: Actually, looking at the yt-feed code more carefully:
4248: 
4249: ```tsx
4250: const cached = loadCookie()
4251: if (cached) {
4252:   try {
4253:     const tube = await Innertube.create({ cookie: cached, cache: new UniversalCache(true) })

4261: 
4262: At startup, it checks if cookie file exists. If so, validates it. Sets `cookieStr = cached` on success.

4264: If no cookie at startup, `cookieStr` stays null forever — even if the file is written later.
4265: 
4266: The "feed" method handler:
4267: ```tsx
4268: if (method === "feed") {
4269:   if (!cookieStr) { send(reqId, null, "Not authenticated"); return }
4270:   const tube = await Innertube.create({ cookie: cookieStr, cache: new UniversalCache(true) })
4271:   ...
4272: }
4273: ```
4274: 
4275: It only uses `cookieStr` (the cached startup value), never re-reads the file.
4276: 
4277: **The fix**: In the "feed" handler, re-read the cookie file each time, or at least check if it exists and try to load it if `cookieStr` is null:
4278: 
4279: ```tsx
4280: if (method === "feed") {
4281:   if (!cookieStr) {
4282:     const fresh = loadCookie()
4283:     if (fresh) {
4284:       try {
4285:         const tube = await Innertube.create({ cookie: fresh, cache: new UniversalCache(true) })
4286:         await tube.account.getInfo()
4287:         cookieStr = fresh
4288:       } catch {
4289:         send(reqId, null, "Not authenticated"); return
4290:       }
4291:     } else {
4292:       send(reqId, null, "Not authenticated"); return
4293:     }
4294:   }
4295:   const tube = await Innertube.create({ cookie: cookieStr, cache: new UniversalCache(true) })
4296:   ...
4297: }

4300: Or simpler: just always re-read the cookie in the "feed" handler (don't cache it in a module-level variable):
4301: 
4302: ```tsx

4304:   const cookie = loadCookie()
4305:   if (!cookie) { send(reqId, null, "Not authenticated"); return }

4307:   ...

4311: But that would re-create `Innertube` on every request even if the cookie hasn't changed, which is wasteful. Better to lazy-load: if `cookieStr` is null, try to read the file.

4313: The cleanest fix for yt-feed/main.ts's "feed" handler:
4314: 
4315: ```tsx

1044: 791: 
1045: 792: ## All Key Decisions Made (Chronological)
1046: 793: 
1047: 794: ### Architecture Decisions
1048: 795: 1. **Language-agnostic plugin system** — plugins can be written in any language (Go, Python, etc.)
1049: 796: 2. **Subprocess stdin/stdout JSON-RPC** — simplest cross-language IPC. Each plugin is a standalone process
1050: 797: 3. **No `jsonrpc` field** — messages are `{"id", "method", "params"}` only, cleaner than full JSON-RPC spec
1051: 798: 4. **Host routes by method prefix** — `"greet."` matches `"greet.hello"`. Plugin handles the specific action
1052: 799: 5. **Desktop first, mobile later** — subprocess works on desktop. Mobile will need FFI/Wasm
1053: 800: 6. **Different skeleton per platform is fine** — Electrobun for desktop, Tauri/zero-native for mobile. Plugins don't change
1054: 801: 7. **Everything is a plugin** — including frontend UI and eventually the skeleton itself
1055: 802: 8. **No "core" plugin** — just feature plugins (no separate plugin for core system functionality)
1056: 803: 9. **Companion app** (future) — a tiny binary that reads config and launches the right skeleton for the platform
1057: 804: 10. **Manifest scanning from plugins/*/plugin.json** — replaced config.json. Host reads all plugin.json files at startup via readdirSync + JSON.parse. No central config needed.
1058: 805: 11. **Flat manifest format** — no nested backend/frontend objects. All fields at top level. Matches VS Code/Chrome/Obsidian conventions.
1059: 806: 
1060: 807: ### Framework Decisions
1061: 808: 12. **Electrobun for prototyping** — easiest for a beginner (Bun/TypeScript). Native WebView, ~14MB bundle, fast startup
1062: 809: 13. **Tauri for future mobile** — Rust, mature ecosystem, iOS + Android support, but requires learning Rust
1063: 810: 14. **zero-native** (Vercel Labs) — alternative future option. Zig + system WebView, mobile support, but pre-release (v0.2)
1064: 811: 15. **WebUI (webui-dev)** — interesting but no mobile path. Opens a real browser (Chrome/Firefox), not a WebView. Few KB library
1065: 812: 16. **React + Tailwind + Vite** for the frontend (from the Electrobun template)
1066: 813: 
1067: 814: ### Phase 3 Decisions
1068: 815: 17. **Feed approach is THE approach** — old per-plugin widget cards are dead. App.tsx mounts only `<feed-widget>`. No WebComponentSlot, no plugin cards, no callMethod, no result box.
1069: 816: 18. **No library sharing needed** — one WC class definition is shared across all DOM instances. Framework bundle lives in prototype. Different plugins have different bundles (their own versions). No duplication within the same WC type. Option B (per-plugin shared library) solves a non-problem.
1070: 817: 19. **No `host.*` routing** — feed-widget does NOT call host RPCs. App.tsx calls host directly (`electroview.rpc.request.getPluginManifests({})`) and passes data via `.manifests` setter on the WC DOM element. `__pluginRpc` bridge stays simple: routes only to plugin subprocesses.
1071: 818: 20. **No fallback cards** — postponed. Only cards from plugins are rendered. Items from plugins without `card` field are skipped.
1072: 819: 21. **Data flow via property setters** — App.tsx uses `.manifests` setter, feed-widget uses `.item` setter on each card. Not via RPC, not via events.
1073: 820: 22. **`_item` naming convention** — private backing field with underscore prevents infinite loop in setter. `set item(data) { this._item = data; this._render() }`. Getter: `get item() { return this._item }`.
1074: 821: 23. **Simplified manifest** — `run` replaces `command`+`args`. `feeds` block replaces `frontendComponent`/`frontendFile`/`frontendSlot`. `ui` field for main-UI WC (only feed plugin uses it). No backward compat with old format.
1075: 822: 24. **Path derivation** — frontend file paths NOT in manifest. Derived at runtime: `plugins/<name>/frontend/<tag>.js`. Tag comes from `ui` or `feeds.card` field.
1076: 823: 25. **Feed is a plugin** — `plugins/feed/` with no backend. Users can swap feed implementation by installing a different feed plugin.
1077: 824: 26. **Framework agnostic cards** — each card WC is self-contained IIFE with framework inlined. React, Preact, Vue, Svelte all work.
1078: 825: 27. **No schema** — feed doesn't know or care about item structure. Raw data passes through to card WC. Cards written by the same person as the backend.
1079: 826: 28. **Auth in error banners** — feed-widget shows "Sign in" button in per-plugin error banners when plugin has `.auth.login` method. Calls it, reloads feed on success.
1080: 827: 29. **5 feed states** — loading, system error, empty, partial (some errors), loaded (all ok). Error banners per-plugin.
1081: 828: 
1082: 829: ### Plugin Design Decisions
1083: 830: 17. **Web Components for frontend plugins** — any framework (React, Vue, Svelte, Angular) can compile to them. Browser standard, no framework lock-in
1084: 831: 18. **Iframes as alternative** — stronger isolation, separate JS context, communication via postMessage. Heavier. Cannot display native UI (Qt/GTK)
1085: 832: 19. **Three plugin types** — `backend` (subprocess only), `frontend` (Web Component only), `fullstack` (both)
1086: 833: 20. **`window.__pluginRpc()` global bridge** — simplest way for any WC framework to call backend. No imports needed.
1087: 834: 21. **Centralized build script** — `scripts/build-plugins.js` handles all plugin types. One command for all.
1088: 835: 22. **`findProjectRoot()` walks up from `import.meta.dir`** — works in both dev (flat) and bundled modes
1089: 836: 23. **FileSink.write() for plugin stdin** — Bun's `Subprocess.stdin` is a `FileSink` when piped. Use `.write()` directly.
1090: 837: 24. **RPC params typed as `unknown`** — Electrobun's `defineRPC` expects `(params?: unknown) => unknown`. All handlers cast internally.
1091: 838: 
1092: 839: ### Go Plugin Specific
1093: 840: 25. **`*json.RawMessage` for params** — user explicitly chose this over simpler `map[string]interface{}`. More type safety, more verbose.
1094: 841: 26. **Nested struct for params** — each method defines its own params struct, unmarshals from RawMessage
1095: 842: 
1096: 843: ### Teaching/Communication Decisions
1097: 844: 27. **User is a beginner** — assume ZERO prior knowledge. Explain every concept, syntax, and line
1098: 845: 28. **Provide full code in messages** — user copies code themselves. Never modify files without explicit permission
1099: 846: 29. **Line-by-line explanation tables** — after every code block, explain each section in a table
1100: 847: 30. **Multi-level zoom** — big picture → file → scope/block → line → symbol → syntax construct
1101: 848: 31. **Be proactive** — research tools, patterns, pitfalls without being asked. Suggest better approaches
1102: 849: 32. **Mentor, not yes-man** — correct wrong assumptions directly. Lead the project in the right direction
1103: 850: 33. **Test standalone before integrating** — catch plugin bugs in isolation before running the full app
1104: 851: 34. **No code comments unless asked** — don't add comments to code files
1105: 852: 35. **Plan mode = read-only, Build mode = can write** — plan mode explains and provides code in messages, build mode can create/edit files + run commands
1106: 853: 36. **Never commit unless asked** — no git operations without explicit instruction
1107: 854: 37. **Two-file rule** — only modify AGENTS.md (project knowledge) and SKILL.md (general rules). Never touch project code.
1108: 855: 38. **Update both files every prompt** — actively check for changes. Never assume "last agent handled it."
1109: 856: 
1110: 857: ### Session 2026-07-07 Decisions (Plugin Refactor — youtube-explorer split, hooks, components, feeds array)
1111: 858: 39. **`components` manifest field** — separates build concern from mount concern. `ui` → build AND mount (views). `components` → build only (cards, sub-components). Fixes the Single-Field Conflation Antipattern where `ui` was the only way to trigger a build.
1112: 859: 40. **`hooks` manifest field** — decentralized capability discovery. A plugin declares what hooks it satisfies (e.g., `"feed.video"`, `"auth"`, `"search"`, `"player"`). The host resolves hooks at runtime. Replaces hardcoded method prefix routing for capability discovery.
1113: 860: 41. **`callHook`/`resolveHook` RPC handlers** — new host RPCs for hook-based discovery. `callHook` finds the first plugin matching a hook and calls its method. Enables feed-widget to use `callHook("feed.video")` instead of iterating manifests.
1114:

1156: 24: ## How HMR Works

1159: 27: 
1160: 28: 1. **Vite dev server** starts on `http://localhost:5173` with HMR enabled
1161: 29: 2. **Electrobun** starts and detects the running Vite server

1163: 31: 4. Changes to React components update instantly without full page reload

1166: 34:
